items.body: ## Summary `client_secret_expires_at` never reached the database. The `oauthClient` schema has had no column for it since the plugin landed, although `SchemaClient` and both mappers expect `expiresAt`. Managed registration also replaced the admin's value with `0`. Every response reported `0`, and a secret past its expiry kept authenticating, contrary to the "Create Client" and "Dynamic Client Registration Expiration" docs and [RFC 7591 §3.2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-3.2.1). ```diff persistOAuthClientRegistration dynamic → clientRegistrationClientSecretExpiration ?? 0 - managed → 0 + managed → admin's client_secret_expires_at ?? 0 - adapter.create # expiresAt dropped, no column + adapter.create # new optional oauthClient.expiresAt validateClientCredentials # token, introspect, revoke verify secret + expiresAt <= now → invalid_client "client secret has expired" ``` - Expiry is checked only after the secret matches, so a caller without the secret learns nothing about it, and `private_key_jwt` clients are never affected. - A string value is a time span from now (`"90d"`), as in `clientRegistrationClientSecretExpiration`. Any other string returns 400 `invalid_client_metadata`. - `adminUpdateOAuthClient` with `0` clears the expiry. Rotation keeps it, so a client owner cannot outlast an admin-set expiry. ## Evidence New `client-secret-expiry.test.ts`, through `auth.api` and `auth.handler`: ```text registerOAuthClient with clientRegistrationClientSecretExpiration: "30d" main: client_secret_expires_at 0, no stored expiresAt now: issued_at + 30d in the response, the row, and getOAuthClient adminCreateOAuthClient { client_secret_expires_at: now - 3600 }, then client_credentials main: response reports 0 now: 401 invalid_client ``` - **Before:** 5 of 6 fail on `main`. **After:** 6 of 6 pass. Reverting only the `validateClientCredentials` check turns both `invalid_client` tests red. The oauth-provider suite (1026 tests) and `pnpm typecheck` pass. ## Merge Danger **Door:** one-way The `expiresAt` column lands in users' databases, so renaming or removing it later takes another migration. **Blast Radius:** migration - `minor` changeset, so release automation moves this to `next`. - The column must exist before deploy. Prisma and Drizzle read every declared column, so deploying a regenerated client or schema before migrating breaks every OAuth client read, with or without an expiry. Until the column exists, writes that carry an expiry also fail: admin create or update with `client_secret_expires_at`, and every dynamic registration that issues a client secret when `clientRegistrationClientSecretExpiration` is set. This is read from the adapter code; only SQLite ran. - Clients registered before the upgrade have no stored expiry and still never expire. --- ## Summary by cubic Persists and enforces OAuth client secret expiry. Previously the value was dropped, every response reported `client_secret_expires_at: 0`, and a secret past its expiry kept authenticating. The expiry now saves to a new optional `oauthClient.expiresAt` column, reports in registration and read responses, and makes the token, introspection, and revocation endpoints reject an expired secret with `invalid_client` (only after the secret matches). Managed registration keeps the admin-set expiry, `adminUpdateOAuthClient` clears it with `0`, rotation preserves it, and string values like `"90d"` are read as time spans from now; empty strings, non-time-span strings, and out-of-range values are rejected with `invalid_client_metadata`. **Related fixes** - DPoP proofs validate against the concrete request path, resolving route params (e.g. `/extension/acme/token`) and keeping trailing slashes when `advanced.skipTrailingSlashes` is on. - New `allowClientKeyRotation` option lets `private_key_jwt` clients with inline `jwks` replace their own signing keys via `POST /oauth2/client/rotate-keys`. Off by default; refuses to start on the memory adapter or with `generateId: "serial"`. - Updates, deletes, and secret rotations of clients listed in `cachedTrustedClients` now return `invalid_client` with HTTP 400 instead of 500. - Adds black-box DPoP interop smoke tests using `oauth4webapi` and forces both orderings of the revoke-vs-rotate refresh race in tests. **Migration** This adds a nullable column to the `oauthClient` table. Run `npx auth@latest migrate` with the built-in Kysely adapter, or `npx auth@latest generate` and apply the change with Prisma or Drizzle, migrating before deploying the regenerated client or schema; MongoDB needs nothing. Until the column exists, writes carrying an expiry fail and dynamic registration fails when `clientRegistrationClientSecretExpiration` is set. Clients registered before the upgrade have no stored expiry and still never expire. Written for commit 56e3c0441b0c4120f55b1dcfc46a29ecf65909d7. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(db): ensure atomic deleteUser and propagate pre-read errors in deleteWithHooks

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

items.body:
## What
- In `deleteWithHooks` and `deleteManyWithHooks` (`packages/better-auth/src/db/with-hooks.ts`), removed error-swallowing `try/catch` blocks around `findMany` queries so database connectivity, query, and driver failures propagate rather than being masked as empty results.
- In `internalAdapter.deleteUser` (`packages/better-auth/src/db/internal-adapter.ts`), wrapped cascading deletions of sessions, accounts, and user rows inside `runWithTransaction(adapter, ...)` to ensure ACID atomicity across all operations.
- Preserved child delete hooks execution before user deletion, preventing foreign-key cascades from preempting session and account hooks while cleanly respecting hook vetoes via transactional rollback (`VetoRollbackError`).
- Registered secondary storage session cache eviction (`queueCachedUserSessionDeletion`) first inside `runWithTransaction`, guaranteeing cache eviction executes upon commit even if user-defined child after-hooks throw.
- Rebased branch onto latest `origin/main`.

## Why
Resolves #11667.
1. When `findMany` threw an error during `deleteWithHooks`, the `try/catch` swallowed it, leaving `entityToDelete = null`. This caused `adapter.delete` to be skipped while returning `null` without error, causing `/delete-user` to report `{ success: true, message: "User deleted" }` even though the user row remained intact in the database.
2. Deletions of sessions, accounts, and the user in `deleteUser` were separate uncoordinated queries without transaction wrapping. If deleting the user failed (e.g. FK lock, timeout, cancellation), sessions and accounts were already permanently deleted, corrupting user state.
3. If an after-hook threw post-commit, secondary storage cache cleanup was previously skipped. Ensuring cache cleanup runs first guarantees stale sessions are never served from Redis.

## Linked Issue
Fixes #11667

## Breaking Changes
NONE

## Testing Performed
- Added comprehensive regression and invariant tests in `packages/better-auth/src/db/with-hooks.test.ts` (9 tests passed):
  * DB query error propagation in `deleteWithHooks` and `deleteManyWithHooks`.
  * Missing/non-existent entity return contract (returns `null` safely without Prisma P2025 errors).
  * `/delete-user` endpoint error reporting when pre-read fails.
  * Atomic transaction rollback of sessions and accounts when user deletion fails (verifying writes occurred inside transaction and rolled back).
  * Veto rollback tests for both user and session delete hooks.
  * Secondary storage cache eviction resilience when child after-hooks throw.
- Executed existing test suites to ensure zero regressions:
  * `packages/better-auth/src/db/secondary-storage.test.ts` (all 21 passed).
  * `packages/better-auth/src/db/db.test.ts` (`delete hooks` passed).
  * `packages/better-auth/src/db/internal-adapter.test.ts` (all 72 passed).
  * `packages/better-auth/src/api/routes/update-user.test.ts` (all 34 passed).
- Full monorepo typecheck passed (`pnpm typecheck`).

## Risk Tier
Medium

## Rollback Plan
`git revert HEAD` (reverts cleanly with no schema migrations).

## Reviewer Notes
The fix preserves the Prisma P2025 fix from PR #7792 (`shouldRunAdapterDelete && entityToDelete` check) so that when a row does not exist (`findMany` returns `[]`), it continues to safely return `null` without throwing. Only genuine query errors (where `findMany` rejects) now propagate.

## API Delta
NONE

items.title: fix(api-key): use the active transaction's adapter

labels.name: payments
labels.description: Stripe, API keys, subscriptions

items.body: ## Summary The api-key plugin calls `ctx.context.adapter` directly. Those calls bypass the transaction adapter that `runWithTransaction` puts in async context, so inside a transaction the plugin writes outside it: - On a pooled database such as PostgreSQL, a key created, updated, or deleted through the plugin uses another connection and survives a rollback. - On a single-connection database such as in-memory SQLite, the plugin's write waits for the transaction's lock and the call hangs until it times out. This PR routes the plugin's adapter calls through `getCurrentAdapter(ctx.context.adapter)`, as the internal adapter already does. Outside a transaction, `getCurrentAdapter` returns the same adapter, so behavior is unchanged. ## Why it matters Applications that create a key together with related rows need both writes to commit or roll back together. Examples include an audit entry, a service account, or an ownership record. Today the key row commits even when the surrounding transaction fails. ```ts await runWithTransaction(ctx.adapter, async () => { await auth.api.createApiKey({ body: { userId, name: "integration" } }); await (await getCurrentAdapter(ctx.adapter)).create({ model: "auditEvent", data }); // if this throws, the key is still persisted before this change }); ``` ## Changes - `packages/api-key/src/adapter.ts`, `org-authorization.ts`, and the create, update, delete, and verify routes use `(await getCurrentAdapter(ctx.context.adapter))` for every adapter call. Reads are included so that a key written earlier in the same transaction is visible to later calls in it. - `packages/api-key/src/api-key-transaction.test.ts` covers three cases: - a key created in a transaction that rolls back is discarded; - a key created in a transaction that commits is kept; - an update in a transaction that rolls back is discarded. - A patch changeset for `@better-auth/api-key`. ## Testing `pnpm vitest packages/api-key --run`: 196 tests pass. Without the source change, the three new tests time out on in-memory SQLite. `tsc --build packages/api-key` and `biome check` pass. --- Generated with AI 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the api-key plugin bypassing the active transaction so keys created, updated, or deleted inside `runWithTransaction` now commit and roll back with it. The plugin called `ctx.context.adapter` directly, ignoring the transaction adapter that `runWithTransaction` puts in async context. On pooled databases like PostgreSQL, a key write used a different connection and survived a rollback. On single-connection databases like in-memory SQLite, the write waited on the transaction's lock and timed out. All adapter calls now route through `getCurrentAdapter(ctx.context.adapter)`. Outside a transaction this returns the same adapter, so behavior is unchanged there. **Secondary storage** - With `fallbackToDatabase`, rows read or touched inside a transaction are never cached: cache writes are deferred until it commits and cached entries are invalidated while it is open. - Verification rejects a key disabled in the database even if secondary storage still holds an enabled copy. - A failed post-commit cache write is logged instead of failing a request whose database change already succeeded. - Deferred expired/exhausted-key cleanup runs with the root adapter and only deletes keys still expired or exhausted, so a key restored by a rollback survives. Tests in `packages/api-key/src/api-key-transaction.test.ts` cover rolled-back and committed creates, updates, and a delete, deferred cleanup, cache invalidation, and cache-write failures. A patch changeset for `@better-auth/api-key` is included. Written for commit 5a2adcfd87b5a1497c68ddc11ae68274a6165d23. Summary will update on new commits.

### Is this suited for github?

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Right now, better-auth uses fixed roles and permissions, making it hard for admins to change access rights without updating code or planning everything ahead.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add a way for admins to create and change roles and permissions easily, like the organization plugin, using a simple dashboard or API. Store the settings in a database.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

We looked into using a different access control system, but it would require starting from scratch and wouldn’t fit well with better-auth.

### Additional context

related discussion: https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1357026607033880727
---

## Adopted as tracking issue: 2026-04-14

## Scope clarification
This issue tracks dynamic roles and their lifecycle for the admin plugin: create, rename, remove defaults, validate custom roles, and signal client-side staleness. It does not track platform admin scope, impersonation, team-role assignment, or permission-union math; those items belong in `tracking: admin plugin: super-admin scope, impersonation, permission math`.

## In scope
- Dynamic role create / update / delete.
- Role rename consistency across the member table (#7727).
- Removing defaults (#6772, #8604 owner-role missing).
- Custom role validation (#9156 `dash` plugin flagging).
- Client-side invalidation of role state on sign-out and role change (#8595 cross-ref to session cookie cache).
- TS surface for dynamic-role operations (the invite-endpoint variant #9135 and the admin-plugin-wide pattern).

## Out of scope
- Super-admin vs org-admin authority (#1595), impersonation (#3056, #7796), team-role (#4493), permission-union math (#3011): `tracking: admin plugin: super-admin scope, impersonation, permission math`.
- General TypeScript inference gaps that surface at role-adjacent endpoints: `tracking: TypeScript inference` (#5666).

## Resolution criteria
- Dynamic roles create and rename propagate to member rows.
- Built-in roles can be disabled entirely.
- Custom role validation reports cleanly to all plugins that inspect roles.
- Client-side role state invalidates on sign-out without manual refetch.
- Dynamic-role operations typecheck across all endpoints that accept a role input.

items.title: feat(auth): add explicit confirmation mode for delete-user links

labels.name: core
labels.description: Core infra, API routes, session, cookies, client SDK

labels.name: devtools
labels.description: CLI, OpenAPI, telemetry, i18n, test-utils

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Documentation, demos

items.body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `user.deleteUser.confirmationMode: "instant" | "explicit"`. In `"explicit"` mode the emailed delete-account link no longer deletes the account just by being opened.

Closes #11527

## Problem

With `sendDeleteAccountVerification` configured, the emailed link points at `GET /delete-user/callback?token=...`, and that request deletes the account in the same call. A state-changing `GET` can be fired by things other than the user: mail clients that prefetch links, Outlook Safe Links, corporate proxies and scanners that open every URL in a message.

## Changes

- `user.deleteUser.confirmationMode` (default `"instant"`, current behavior unchanged).
- In `"explicit"` mode, the `url` passed to `sendDeleteAccountVerification` is the app's own URL (built from `callbackURL`) with `token` attached.
- `callbackURL` is validated before the token is created, so a rejected request leaves no orphaned verification row. It must be an absolute URL with a safe scheme, must not point back at `/delete-user/callback` (however its path is written: trailing slash, query, fragment, dot segments, percent-encoding, double encoding; the base path is canonicalized the same way), and must not already carry a `token` query parameter, since the real token is appended. Otherwise the request fails with `CALLBACK_URL_REQUIRED` or `INVALID_CALLBACK_URL`.
- `GET /delete-user/preview`: validates the token and returns the pending user without deleting.
- `POST /delete-user/confirm`: body `{ token, password? }`, consumes the token and deletes, through the same path as the instant callback (`beforeDelete` / `afterDelete` hooks included). `password` re-verifies the user at confirmation time, which a link click can't do.
- Both endpoints need the signed-in user the token was issued for. They read the session through `getAuthoritativeSessionFromCtx`, so a revoked session that an earlier hook loaded from the cookie cache can't preview or confirm a deletion. I reproduced that with a test (a hook that preloads the cached session, a revoked session row and a valid cached cookie) before fixing it; `confirm` deleted the account.
- `confirm` validates ownership and expiry before consuming the token, so a token that belongs to another user, or has expired, isn't burned by a request that can't use it. It also rejects passwords longer than `maxPasswordLength` before hashing.
- `/delete-user/confirm` is added to the client's session signal, so the client refreshes its session after a confirmed deletion.
- The deletion itself moved into a shared `performDeleteUser`, used by the callback and `confirm`.
- The `callbackURL` validation lives in a small shared helper, `utils/confirmation-url.ts`. It is the same file, with the same tests, that the change-email, transfer-ownership and organization-deletion PRs add, so they merge cleanly in any order.

## Notes for review

- No schema changes: it reuses the existing `delete-account-*` verification record. No breaking changes; without `confirmationMode`, nothing changes.
- For HTTP requests, the origin of `callbackURL` is checked against `trustedOrigins` by the existing origin middleware (`INVALID_ORIGIN` for the request's origin, `INVALID_CALLBACK_URL` for the `callbackURL`). Direct `auth.api.deleteUser` calls skip that check, and the docs say so.
- `GET /delete-user/preview` and `POST /delete-user/confirm` are registered in both modes. They need the same session and token the instant callback does, so they don't grant anything new.
- `deleteUserCallback` (the instant link) still uses its existing session read. That's behavior already on `main`, so I left it out of this PR.
- The OpenAPI snapshot is updated for the two new endpoints.

## Tests

In `update-user.test.ts`:

- explicit mode: the emailed link is app-owned, preview doesn't delete, only `confirm` does
- a wrong password on `confirm` doesn't burn the token
- missing, relative, callback-pointing (plain, trailing slash, query/fragment, dot segments) `callbackURL`s are rejected and no token is created
- preview and `confirm` reject requests without a session
- another signed-in user can't use, or burn, someone else's token
- unknown and expired tokens are rejected, and `deleteUser.enabled: false` returns 404
- over-long passwords are rejected before hashing
- concurrent `confirm` calls delete once, and the hooks run once
- a revoked session with a valid cached cookie is rejected by preview and confirm, with a hook that preloads the session

Unit tests for the URL helper (percent-encoded and double-encoded paths, malformed escapes, existing `token`, base-path canonicalization, legitimate paths with encoded characters) and for the client session signal.

## Changeset

`better-auth`, `@better-auth/core`: `patch`

items.body: **Summary** Align error response codes for email validation across authentication endpoints to allow granular client-side error handling. **Problem** The endpoints `/api/auth/sign-up/email` and `/api/auth/change-email` currently fail schema validation at the request body layer, returning a generic `VALIDATION_ERROR`. This prevents clients from catching specific validation issues and presenting user-friendly error messages (e.g., distinguishing between a missing required field and an ill-formed email address or showing a correct translation of the error). *Current Response:* ```json { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "Validation error", "originalMessage": "[body.email] Invalid email address" } ``` **Solution** * Loosened the body schema for these endpoints to validate the payload as a string rather than enforcing strict email format rules at the schema layer. * Moved email format verification directly into the endpoint implementation logic (matching the pattern used by other auth endpoints). * Updated error responses to return a specific `INVALID_EMAIL` error code upon failure. *New Response:* ```json { "code": "INVALID_EMAIL", "message": "Ungültige E-Mail-Adresse", "originalMessage": "Invalid email" } ``` --- ## Summary by cubic Changes email validation on the sign-up and change-email endpoints to return a specific `INVALID_EMAIL` error code instead of the generic `VALIDATION_ERROR`, so clients can distinguish an ill-formed email from other validation failures. - Loosens the request body schema to accept any non-empty string for the email field. - Moves email format verification into the endpoint logic, matching other auth endpoints. - Endpoints now return a single error at a time instead of an array of all validation errors. Written for commit 1aa74fbb7cabd6f97768f33d4bded730745ce3b4. Summary will update on new commits.

items.body: `baseURL` did two unrelated jobs. It was the stable identity of the auth server (OAuth/OIDC issuer, JWT `iss`/`aud`, social-login `redirect_uri`, Passkey relying-party id), and in its object form it was also a per-request allowlist for picking which host to build URLs against. That object's `allowedHosts` were already folded into `trustedOrigins`, so the allowlist lived in two places. Per-request resolution was written three times, in the HTTP handler, the `auth.api` path, and the MCP handler, and a config shape added to one was silently unhandled by the others. This splits the two jobs. `baseURL` is the canonical origin and nothing reads it per request. The extra hosts a deployment serves live in `trustedOrigins`, which already accepts a static array or a per-request function. A single boundary resolver computes the per-request serving origin, the request's host when it is trusted and the canonical origin otherwise, and every entry point goes through it. Cookies and self-referential links (email verification, magic links, password reset) then follow the host the request arrived on, while identity stays fixed. Letting identity follow the request host was an active hazard, not just redundancy. A Passkey registered against a `*.vercel.app` preview is bound to that ephemeral host and breaks on the next deploy, and an OIDC token would carry an issuer that no longer resolves. Identity is canonical by default. Running a genuinely per-tenant issuer or rp id means setting that concern's own option (`jwt.issuer`, the OAuth Provider issuer, Passkey `rpID`, or `oAuthProxy.productionURL`) to a per-request value. Closes #4151. Closes #8478. Closes #8548. --- ## Summary by cubic Make `baseURL` the canonical origin for identity and move multi-host serving to `trustedOrigins`, with one per-request resolver shared by all entry points. Cookies and links follow the trusted request host; issuer/JWT/redirect_uri/Passkey rpID stay anchored to `baseURL`. - **New Features** - Removed object form of `baseURL`; it’s now a string canonical origin only. - Unified per-request origin resolver (`resolvePerRequestContext` / `getRequestBaseURL`) used by the HTTP handler, routes, and direct `auth.api` calls; export `getRequestBaseURL`. - If the request host is in `trustedOrigins`, cookies and self-referential links use that host; otherwise they fall back to `baseURL`. The serving origin comes from `Host` by default; `x-forwarded-*` headers are ignored unless `advanced.trustedProxyHeaders: true`. - Updated docs, tests, and internal calls; removed dynamic baseURL types and helpers. - **Migration** - Replace `baseURL: { allowedHosts, protocol, fallback }` with: - `baseURL: "https://auth.example.com"` (canonical origin). - `trustedOrigins: [...]` or `trustedOrigins: (ctx) => [...]` for extra hosts. - If identity must vary per tenant, set the specific option per request: - `jwt.issuer`, OAuth Provider issuer, Passkey `rpID`, or `oAuthProxy.productionURL`. - If your proxy only exposes the public hostname via forwarded headers, set `advanced.trustedProxyHeaders: true`. Written for commit 8dffad64a75ba62191c32393898abe87e87e9cf5. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(oauth-provider): replay concurrent refresh grants inside reuse interval

labels.name: identity
labels.description: OAuth/OIDC provider, device flow

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Documentation, demos

items.body: Fixes #12087 ### Description `refreshTokenReuseInterval` already replayed a sequential retry of a rotated refresh token. Two `refresh_token` grants with the same parent at the same time still produced one `200` and one `400 invalid_grant`, including on `mcp()` (default interval 30s). The rotation CAS revokes the parent before `storeRefreshTokenRotationReplay` writes. The loser either failed the CAS in `createRefreshToken` or read a revoked parent with no replay yet. When the reuse interval is set, the second request now waits on the parent row until the stored replay appears (or the short wait expires / the request does not match), then returns the same tokens as a sequential retry. Strict mode (`refreshTokenReuseInterval: 0`) is unchanged. This does not change `invalidateRefreshFamily` and is intentionally separate from #12159 (grant-family teardown scope). ### Test plan - `pnpm vitest packages/oauth-provider/src/token.test.ts packages/mcp/src/plugin.test.ts --run` - Concurrent reuse-interval tests fail on main, pass on this branch - Existing "rejects concurrent rotation of the same refresh token" (no reuse interval) still expects one `invalid_grant` This contribution was written with an AI coding agent and reviewed by me. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #12087: two overlapping `refresh_token` grants for the same parent returned one `200` and one `400 invalid_grant` even inside `refreshTokenReuseInterval` — including on `mcp()`, which defaults the interval to 30s. The rotation CAS revokes the parent before the winner stores its replay, so the loser either lost the CAS or read a revoked parent with no replay yet. When the reuse interval is set, the losing request now polls the parent row (in 25ms steps) for the winner's stored replay and returns the same rotated tokens as a sequential retry, instead of failing closed. Recovery only fires for the dedicated CAS-in-flight error, so an unrelated `invalid_grant` — such as a callback failure — is never replaced with another request's tokens. The wait deadline is the reuse window (`rotationReplayExpiresAt`), not a fixed cap. During recovery, DPoP-bound grants reuse the already-verified binding carried on the in-flight error instead of re-verifying the proof, so a slow rotation cannot fail `proofMaxAgeSeconds`. If the winner's issuance or replay storage fails, the parent is marked unavailable so concurrent retries return `invalid_grant` immediately instead of polling out the reuse window. **Notes** - Adds concurrent-refresh tests for the OAuth provider (including DPoP, a slow-winner wait past 2s, an isolated proof max-age window, and failed replay storage) and the MCP plugin. - `invalidateRefreshFamily` behavior is unchanged; this stays separate from the grant-family teardown scope. Written for commit f8f9ffe7b88d2aad627fbe39c8583bd63491b4ef. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: feat(organizations): [WIP] Add support for roles in teams

labels.name: organization
labels.description: Org, teams, roles, permissions, admin, access control

items.body: **PR is WIP, collaboration is more than welcome.** --- Previously, role-based access control (RBAC) in the organization plugin are only granted on an organization level. This is suboptimal for many B2B SaaS setups, and I'm finding myself missing this feature in my own infrastructure. This PR aligns the Teams feature with the organization plugin's core access control model by introducing: - Team-level multi-role support (0..n roles per team member). - Adds a scope to access control, including dynamic access control (scope: "organization" | "team" | "both"). - Privilege escalation protections between organization-level and team-level scopes. - Permission statements stays flat, it's only roles that pertain to *either* teams or organizations - or both when relevant. The objective is to allow providers to manage sub-resources within a single organization (tenant). ## Business case example: Expense app In Business Expense App X, there's four main types of users; - Finance Admins (organization owner, oversees and manages all) - Department Manager (organization member, team owner) - Department Approver (organization member, team member, specific permission of `expense-report:create-approval`) - Employee (organization member, team member) A given user may be an employee who's a member of several teams for expensing purposes, and then acts as an approver of specific teams' expenses, and as a department manager of another team. I'm happy to elaborate on business use cases, if needed. --- This PR would allow these permission to be natively managed through Better-Auth, ensuring that roles can be scoped specifically in their rightful context. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds team-level role support with scoped permissions and privilege escalation protection, extending the organization plugin's access control from organization-only to include team context. - Roles now accept a `scope` of "organization", "team", or "both" via `role()` and `createAccessControl`. - `teamMember` records now store a `role` field, replacing the implicit "member" default. - New endpoints: `list-roles`, `get-role`, and `updateTeamMemberRole`. - Invitations support `teamRole` to assign team roles on acceptance. - Permission checks now consider both org and team roles, with team roles scoped accordingly. - Privilege escalation checks prevent assigning roles with permissions the actor doesn't have. **Migration** - Schema changes: `organizationRole.scope` (default "organization"), `teamMember.role` (default "member"), `invitation.teamRole`. Requires migration for existing data. Written for commit d8bdd5c6e8ed32bd0250537c89f1f2a24a279f85. Summary will update on new commits.

items.body:
`auth.api.changePassword({ revokeOtherSessions: true, ... })` silently rotates the caller's own session, leaving any cached JWT (Convex queries, OIDC consumers) pointing at the deleted session id for ~500 to 1500 ms. The JSDoc on `revokeOtherSessions` reads "revoke all sessions that are not the current one logged in by the user", so the behavior contradicts its own contract.

This PR adds `internalAdapter.deleteOtherSessions(userId, exceptToken)` and routes both `/change-password`'s `revokeOtherSessions: true` branch and `/revoke-other-sessions` through it. `deleteSessions` is unchanged.

items.body:
Closes #10921.

## Summary

- Honor `deferUpdates` for database-backed API-key verification when an `advanced.backgroundTasks.handler` is configured, returning an optimistic result while the authoritative claim runs through that handler.
- Retry stale optimistic quota or rate-limit denials against the authoritative row, rechecking configuration, enabled state, expiry, and requested permissions.
- Claim quota and rate-limit usage together with one exact-snapshot compare-and-set, so a request consumes both allowances or neither under contention.
- Keep secondary-storage fallback cache refresh best-effort after a database claim has committed, invalidating partial cache writes on failure instead of rejecting an already-consumed request.
- Document the eventual-consistency trade-off for deferred updates, including racing policy changes taking effect on the next verification, and the residual non-atomic secondary-storage-only path.

Default behavior is unchanged: `deferUpdates: false`, and `deferUpdates: true` without a background handler, still await the authoritative database claim and return its persisted row.

## Regression coverage

The deterministic tests use `customAPIKeyValidator` and an intercepted `incrementOne` as between-read-and-claim hooks. They cover:

- stale quota and rate-limit recovery;
- concurrent configuration, disable, expiry, and permission changes;
- atomicity in both cross-counter race directions;
- genuine fresh denials and rate-limit details;
- expired-key deletion;
- non-blocking deferred writes; and
- cache refresh failure after a committed database claim.

The rate-limit/quota interleaving regression failed before the atomic claim because quota changed from 2 to 1 even though verification returned `RATE_LIMITED`. It passes after the fix with quota still at 2.

## Validation

- `pnpm vitest packages/api-key/src/api-key.test.ts --run` — 195 passed
- `pnpm --filter @better-auth/api-key typecheck`
- `pnpm exec biome check packages/api-key/src/routes/verify-api-key.ts packages/api-key/src/api-key.test.ts packages/api-key/src/types.ts`
- `pnpm --filter docs exec remark content/docs/plugins/api-key/reference.mdx --frail`
- `pnpm changeset status` — `@better-auth/api-key` included in patch bumps
- `git diff --check`

Codex assisted with reproducing the concurrency failures, developing the deterministic regressions, and reviewing the selective fallback. I reviewed the storage contract, atomic guard set, final diff, and all validation results above.

items.title: fix(telemetry): stop file tracers from shipping every package.json

labels.name: devtools
labels.description: CLI, OpenAPI, telemetry, i18n, test-utils

items.body:
`getPackageVersion` in `packages/telemetry/src/node.ts` reads
`path.join(cwd, "node_modules", pkg, "package.json")`. File tracers such as
`@vercel/nft`, used by Vercel, Next.js standalone output and Netlify, can't
know `pkg` at build time. So they glob `node_modules` and copy every
`package.json` they find into the deployed function. This happens even with
telemetry off, because tracing reads the code without running it.

This PR reads `<dir>/<pkg>/package.json` from each directory in
`require.resolve.paths(pkg)`, the `node_modules` directories Node would
search. nft can't compute those directories statically, so it doesn't glob.

**Behavior.**
- Installed packages still report their installed version.
- A package hoisted to a parent `node_modules`, as in monorepos, is now found.
- Reading the file directly still works when a package's `exports` hides
  `./package.json` (for example `hono` and `drizzle-orm`).
- The declared range in the root package.json is used only when nothing is
  installed. Before, once the root manifest was cached, every later lookup
  returned the declared range and skipped the installed version.
- This code is in the `node` export only; the default export is unchanged.

The new test covers a hoisted package whose `exports` hides `package.json`,
with an app manifest that doesn't declare it. It fails on `main`.

**Measured.** Tracing `dist/node.mjs` with `@vercel/nft` in a project whose
`node_modules` holds about 1,500 `package.json` files:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Traced files | 1,518 | 14 |
| Trace time | ~1s | 20ms |

**Tests.** The new test passes. The telemetry package typecheck and Biome are
clean. The only other failure, `publishes events when enabled`, also fails on
unchanged `main` locally (an auth-config snapshot mismatch).

**Breaking changes.** None.

items.title: fix(adapter): coerce numeric-string and number timestamps to Date on read (#9963)

labels.name: core
labels.description: Core infra, API routes, session, cookies, client SDK

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

items.body: ## Summary Fixes #9963 (scoped). On read, better-auth coerces `date`-typed fields back into `Date` objects, but two coercion sites used a bare `new Date(value)`, which returns `Invalid Date` for a raw epoch-millisecond **string** like `"1774295570569"` (the `Date` string constructor only parses ISO 8601, not numeric strings) and skipped raw `number` values entirely. This silently produced `Invalid Date` at call sites (e.g. the OIDC `max_age` check loops on a session whose `createdAt` came back as a numeric string from a Drizzle + libSQL text column). Closes #9963 ## Root cause Two sites already attempt date coercion on read, both with `new Date(value)`: 1. `packages/core/src/db/adapter/factory.ts` `transformOutput`, gated on `supportsDates === false`, and only checked `typeof === "string"`, so raw `number` was never coerced. 2. `packages/drizzle-adapter/src/drizzle-adapter.ts` `customTransformOutput`, runs unconditionally and is the exact site of the reporter's repro. `new Date("1774295570569")` → `Invalid Date`. ## Fix Add `parseDateValue()` in `packages/core/src/db/adapter/utils.ts` (exported via `@better-auth/core/db/adapter`) that correctly parses ISO strings, numeric-millisecond strings, and raw numbers into a `Date`. Wire it into both existing coercion sites. **Deliberately scoped.** This does NOT change gating logic, adapter contracts, or defaults, it only fixes the two spots that already attempted coercion. The issue's full proposal (coerce every adapter regardless of `supportsDates`, re-hydrate secondary-storage/cookie-cache reads, retire `oauth-provider`'s private timestamp helpers) is an admitted breaking adapter-contract change targeting `next`; that's a maintainer scope decision and is intentionally left out. Every adapter that currently trusts its driver to return `Date` (Prisma, Mongo, Kysely pg/mysql, Memory) is provably untouched. ## Test evidence - RED confirmed pre-fix in `factory.test.ts` (numeric-string → `Invalid Date`; number → not coerced) and in `drizzle-adapter.test.ts` (reproduces the reported symptom). - New `parseDateValue` unit tests in core. - GREEN: `packages/core` 372/372, `packages/drizzle-adapter` 25/25, `packages/kysely-adapter` 21/21 (exercises the `supportsDates:false` branch), `packages/memory-adapter` 16/16, no regressions. - `tsc` clean for both touched packages; Biome clean. --- ## Summary by cubic Coerces numeric-string and number timestamps into real Date objects when reading date fields in `@better-auth/core`’s adapter factory and `@better-auth/drizzle-adapter`. Fixes #9963 and stops OIDC `max_age` loops caused by `Invalid Date`. - Bug Fixes - Added `parseDateValue` in `@better-auth/core/db/adapter` to handle `Date`, number, ISO string, and epoch-millisecond numeric-string inputs; only 9+ digit numeric strings are treated as epoch ms. - Applied in core `transformOutput` when `supportsDates: false` and in `@better-auth/drizzle-adapter` `customTransformOutput`; `Date`, `null`, and `undefined` pass through unchanged; no adapter contract changes. Written for commit 070cf8b343ec85900f46e885a4747defcbc2d701. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: feat(pin): add PIN plugin for step-up authentication

labels.name: core
labels.description: Core infra, API routes, session, cookies, client SDK

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Documentation, demos

items.body:
## Summary

Adds a built-in `pin` plugin for **PIN-based step-up authentication**.

Users can set a hashed PIN and verify it before sensitive actions (transfers, profile changes, re-authentication). A successful verification upgrades the **current** session for a configurable window instead of creating a new session.

### What's included

- `pin.set` — set a PIN (requires the account password by default)
- `pin.change` — change a PIN with the current PIN
- `pin.verify` — verify a PIN and upgrade the current session
- `pin.disable` — remove a PIN (requires the account password by default)
- `pin.status` — report whether a PIN exists and whether the session is stepped up
- Hashed PIN storage using the existing password hasher
- Per-user lockout after consecutive failures plus endpoint rate limiting
- Configurable length, format, step-up TTL, lockout, and password requirements
- Client plugin, docs page, and a changeset

### Design notes

- **No core schema change.** `stepUpExpiresAt` is added to the session by the plugin's own schema, the same way `admin` and `organization` extend the session table. The plugin also adds a `pin` table.
- `pin.verify` sets `stepUpExpiresAt` on the existing session and refreshes the session cookie. It does not create a session or change the user's sign-in state.
- `stepUpExpiresAt` is returned on the session so apps can gate sensitive server actions on it.

```ts
// server
const session = await auth.api.getSession({
  headers: request.headers,
  query: { disableCookieCache: true },
});

if (
  !session?.session.stepUpExpiresAt ||
  new Date(session.session.stepUpExpiresAt) <= new Date()
) {
  throw new Error("STEP_UP_REQUIRED");
}
```

```ts
// client
await authClient.pin.set({ pin: "1234", password });
await authClient.pin.verify({ pin: "1234" });
```

## Testing

- `pnpm vitest packages/better-auth/src/plugins/pin/pin.test.ts --run` — 12 tests passed
- `pnpm typecheck` (repository root) — passed
- `pnpm biome check` on changed files — passed
- `node --import=tsx scripts/validate-sidebar-icons.ts` — passed

## Breaking changes

None. The plugin is opt-in and only adds tables/fields when installed.

## Related issue

Closes #6000

> Note: this is a new feature and the issue has not had a maintainer decision on the final API shape yet. Happy to adjust naming, endpoint surface, or the session-step-up approach during review.

items.title: feat(adapters): support Aurora DSQL with Kysely

labels.name: core
labels.description: Core infra, API routes, session, cookies, client SDK

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Documentation, demos

items.body: ## Summary Aurora DSQL rejects synchronous index creation and can abort otherwise-valid PostgreSQL transactions on concurrent writes. Add opt-in support through the existing Kysely PostgreSQL integration, as proposed in #12088. ```text database: { dialect, type: "postgres", dsql: true } → async indexes, job completion and interrupted-migration recovery → bigint identity IDs with CACHE 1 → bounded 40001 retries for whole transactions and autocommit operations ``` Sign-up verification email and session cookies run after commit, so aborted attempts cannot publish them. Custom transaction callbacks and before hooks must tolerate replay. DSQL-specific migrations and retries require the flag. Includes docs and a patch changeset; no new dependency or standalone adapter. ## Evidence - **Before:** five migration regressions fail; concurrent consumes surface serialization aborts. New signup regressions fail 3/3 without the route fixes. **After:** 186 tests pass (one unrelated skip), including real PostgreSQL migrations/schema detection, DSQL adapter/migration regressions, endpoint replay tests, and transaction hooks. - Full typecheck, 22-package build, repository Biome CI, dependency lint, affected package/type checks, and commit hooks pass. - Live DSQL: CRUD passed for all 40 combined plugin tables (44 foreign keys), four-way single-use consumption and conditional increment, rollback, numeric-ID signup, and three migration-recovery scenarios. Combined async index completion and final OAuth checks are still running. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way for the opt-in runtime; migrations create persistent indexes/identity columns and require normal migration review. **Blast Radius:** auth DSQL retries are bounded; persistent contention still fails. Signup email delivery now occurs after commit, so delivery failure cannot roll back the new user. External SSO, browser passkey ceremonies and payment webhooks are outside the live smoke coverage. This proposes the opt-in design while maintainer feedback on #12088 is pending. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds opt-in Aurora DSQL support to the built-in Kysely PostgreSQL adapter via `database.dsql: true`. Migrations now create indexes with `CREATE INDEX ASYNC` and wait for job completion; interrupted migrations resume pending index jobs. Numeric IDs (`generateId: "serial"`) use `bigint GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY (CACHE 1)`. Confirmed serialization aborts (`40001`) retry the whole transaction or autocommit operation up to three times with backoff; uncertain commit outcomes and other errors propagate immediately. The flag requires PostgreSQL and enabled transactions. Sign-up verification email and session cookies now run only after commit, so aborted attempts can't publish them. Custom transaction callbacks and before-commit hooks may run again on retry, so keep external side effects out of them; queued after-transaction hooks run only after a successful commit. Written for commit a065881ad5e35ebdb5f435be6ebf80dfbc2b9ad3. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(oauth-provider)!: reject repeated OAuth request parameters

labels.name: locked
labels.description: Locked conversations after being closed for 7 days

items.body:
## Summary

The form parser keeps only the last value of a repeated key, so `code=garbage&code=<valid>` returned a token and `scope=read&scope=` reached the grant as an empty scope. [RFC 6749 §3.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.2) requires rejecting repeated parameters and treating an empty one as omitted.

```diff
 POST /oauth2/token | /oauth2/introspect | /oauth2/revoke
   form parser                      # last value wins
   before hooks
+  re-read raw form (formParams)
+    empty value                    → omitted, in any order
+    repeated value                 → 400 invalid_request
+    resource, audience (token)     → array (RFC 8707 §2, RFC 8693 §2.1)
+    value a hook replaced          → kept
   body schema
-    malformed resource             → invalid_request
+    malformed resource             → invalid_target (RFC 8707 §2)
-    validation error               → no Cache-Control
+    validation error               → Cache-Control: no-store
   grant handler
```

A token request with no client authentication still returns `invalid_request`. RFC 6749 §5.2 lists that case under `invalid_client`, but our docs promise `invalid_request` for missing required fields, and node-oidc-provider, fosite and Duende return it too.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `code=a&code=b`, `token=a&token=b` and `scope=m2m:read&scope=` take the last value, and `resource=/api` returns `invalid_request`.
  **After:** `token-request-params.test.ts` and `oauth-endpoint.integration.test.ts` send these as real form requests. Repeats return `invalid_request`, empty values are omitted in both orders, `resource=/api` returns `invalid_target`, and extension grants receive every `audience`. These tests fail on `next` and pass here.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No stored data changes; reverting restores the old parsing.

**Blast Radius:** clients

Clients that send a parameter twice now get `400` instead of a token. Clients matching `invalid_request` for a malformed `resource` get `invalid_target`. A before hook that narrows a repeated `resource` or `audience` must set an array, because a hook value equal to the parser's last value is treated as untouched.

items.body: ## Summary This PR rewrites Better Auth's sign-in and 2FA flow around a paused sign-in model and a method-first two-factor architecture. Instead of creating a session first and then trying to challenge or clean it up in an after-hook, sign-in now resolves to either a finalized session or a paused challenge, and the session is only published once the challenge completes. ## Why The previous matcher-based enforcement was the wrong center of gravity: - it could silently miss new sign-in surfaces - it created sessions before policy ran and then tried to clean them up afterwards - it mixed method state with user-level 2FA enablement, which led to OTP/TOTP inconsistencies and lockout-prone flows - it relied on cookie-cached session state for DB-authoritative 2FA configuration reads This rewrite makes the paused attempt the source of truth, keeps the factor chain on the session, and leaves a safer pattern for other plugins and future auth flows to copy. ## What changed - replace the legacy `twoFactorRedirect` / `challengeId` shape with the generic sign-in challenge envelope and persisted `signInAttempt` - refactor the 2FA plugin around methods, explicit verification state, recovery codes, and shared verification resolution - make paused sign-in attempts atomic and identity-aware, and add per-attempt verification limits and lockout - record `session.amr` and project AMR into OIDC `id_token`; collapse `last-login-method` onto that source of truth - move enforcement to sign-in-time challenge resolution and add `twoFactor({ enforcement: { decide } })` plus the nested `trustDevice` policy surface - move sensitive 2FA configuration reads onto DB-authoritative sessions to fix stale cookie-cache failures - update docs, demo flows, adapter/integration coverage, and end-to-end tests around the new model ## Breaking surface This is a breaking rewrite of the 2FA contract. - paused sign-ins now use the challenge envelope: `{ kind: "challenge", challenge: { kind, attemptId, methods } }` - `trustDeviceMaxAge` is replaced by `trustDevice.{ maxAge, requireReverificationFor }` - `session.amr` becomes the canonical factor chain, and `last-login-method` becomes a thin projection over it ## Fixed and superseded work Closes #9132. This PR also addresses the root cause behind #8627, replaces the matcher-based enforcement from #9122 that was later reverted in #9205, and supersedes the narrower follow-up in #9203 with the model-level rewrite. ## Validation - `pnpm lint` - `pnpm typecheck` - `pnpm test` - `pnpm knip` - `pnpm knip --production` - `demo/nextjs` manual and Playwright validation for sign-up, enrollment, sign-in challenge, OTP verification, and recovery-code fallback --- ## Summary by cubic Refactored sign-in and 2FA around a paused-attempt model with a standard challenge envelope and a single resolver/finalizer that only commits sessions after completion. Sessions now record `amr` and project to OIDC across all sign-in paths (including API keys), improving verification, cookies, and redirects. - **Bug Fixes** - Hardened paused attempts: atomic consume to prevent concurrent completion, cross-user checks when a session exists, and expiry re-check at consume time. - Made recovery-code replacement atomic to avoid partial or empty sets. - Guarded One Tap two-factor fallback redirects with a safe-URL check. - OAuth proxy now catches session-hook `APIErrors` from `resolveSignInWithRedirect` and redirects to the provider’s error URL (e.g., bans), not 500. - Locked `acr_values_supported`/`amr_values_supported` in OIDC discovery and MCP metadata to prevent clobbering. - `appendSignInChallengeToURL` now replaces an existing `challenge` param and keeps details out of the URL; client proxy uses the canonical `isSignInChallenge` guard; `node:sqlite` treats CTE writes as writes. - **Migration** - Replace legacy `twoFactorRedirect`/`challengeId` with the challenge envelope and handle via `isSignInChallenge*` and `appendSignInChallengeToURL`. - Schema: add required `session.amr`; adopt the new `signInAttempt` shape; remove `user.lastLoginMethod` and `SignInAttempt.loginMethod`. - Cookies/options renamed: `dont_remember` → `session_only`; `dontRememberMe` → `rememberMe`; `trustDeviceMaxAge` → `trustDevice.{ maxAge, requireReverificationFor }`; `trust_device` → `trusted_device` (default TTL now 7 days). - 2FA APIs are method-based; “backup codes” are now “recovery codes”; verification modes are `finalize` and `session`. Update flows that assumed a session existed before 2FA. Written for commit d3c97722cd09333496e68f7d8480b16caf5cdd18. Summary will update on new commits.

labels.name: identity

items.body: ## Summary A native app can exchange a live OAuth refresh token for a one-time code, and the browser burns that code for a new session cookie. The exchange is off unless `sessionCode` is set, public clients need no secret, and an access token is rejected. ## Test plan - [ ] `vitest` `oauth session code` in `packages/oauth-provider` - [ ] With `sessionCode: true`, `POST /oauth2/session-code` using `Authorization: Bearer ` returns a code - [ ] `POST /oauth2/session-code/consume` sets a session cookie once, then rejects the same code - [ ] The same call with an access token fails - [ ] The endpoints stay disabled when `sessionCode` is unset --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an opt-in OAuth exchange that lets a native app turn a live refresh token into a one-time code, which a browser then redeems for a new session cookie. This lets a native app open a web account page after the browser session has expired. - Off unless `sessionCode` is set on the OAuth provider options, and configurable with an `expiresIn` code lifetime (default 180 seconds). - `POST /oauth2/session-code` accepts a refresh token in the `Authorization` header and returns a one-time code; no client secret is required and public clients are allowed. - `POST /oauth2/session-code/consume` burns the code to set a session cookie; the same code is rejected on a second use. - Access tokens are rejected; only an unrevoked, unexpired refresh token can mint a code. Written for commit 6ed61e88916eaf788eb4d1bd8c89c8ed20e59bfb. Summary will update on new commits.

items.body: Brings stable fixes from main into the next branch. **This PR must be merged by a maintainer using 'Create a merge commit'** (not squash, not rebase). This preserves individual fix commits and their verified signatures. If there are conflicts, resolve them by keeping next's versions for `package.json` files (next is always ahead of main in version numbers). --- ## Summary by cubic Brings the 1.7.8 stable release from `main` into `next`, covering fixes for type-checking, SCIM, OAuth native redirects, transactional password resets, session caching, and more. This PR must be merged by a maintainer using a merge commit so individual fix commits keep their signatures. - Projects enabling `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` failed to type-check when adding `oauthProvider()` (TS2322) or `mcp()` (TS2430) to `betterAuth()`; both are fixed, along with a TS2536 error in the organization plugin's published types for projects with `skipLibCheck: false`. Fields with `returned: false` are now omitted from inferred output schema types, the Atlassian user info error log now names Atlassian instead of Figma, and OIDC SSO registration rejects a configured issuer that differs from the discovery document, including trailing slash mismatches. SSO provider updates with partial OIDC or SAML mappings no longer fail validation; omitted `email` or `name` fields fall back to the documented defaults, and a mapping that passes `id` is still rejected. OIDC providers that send the email claim as a list, such as Azure AD B2C's `emails`, now use the first address, and Microsoft Entra ID ID-token sign-in and account linking no longer reject every token: Microsoft's signing keys omit `alg`, so they're treated as RS256, and ID tokens now allow 30 seconds of clock skew. SAML providers with linked accounts can rotate their IdP signing certificate again instead of returning 409. The docs clarify the distinction between `callbackUrl` and the ACS endpoint for SAML. - The `@sveltejs/kit` peer range now includes `^3.0.0`, so SvelteKit 3 projects can install without `--legacy-peer-deps`; a SvelteKit 3 e2e fixture, an Effect integration guide, a new community plugin listing, and documentation on SvelteKit 3 imports were added, the JWT docs now list every web key field, plus example-syntax fixes for Electron and Polar. docs also gained a `good-webhooks` community plugin entry and the Effect integration pages, and the header dropdowns now open on activation instead of focus. - Drizzle schemas that store dates in string columns now work: `timestamp({ mode: "string" })`, MySQL `datetime({ mode: "string" })`, and SQLite `text()`, including on Cloudflare D1. Dates are written as UTC text and read back without a time zone as UTC; a behavior change for non-UTC servers is documented in the changeset. - Native OAuth clients and Client ID Metadata Documents now accept custom-scheme redirect URIs with a host and a path, such as Cursor's `cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp/oauth/callback`; previously only the authority-free reverse-domain form was allowed. A new `clientRegistrationDefaultApplicationType` option (`"infer"` or `"native"`) treats dynamic registrations that omit `application_type`, like Cursor, as native; the default remains `"web"`. Admin OAuth client updates now also accept a `disabled` field to pause and resume a client—disabled clients can't obtain new tokens and introspection marks their tokens inactive—and `adminCreateOAuthClient` accepts a `resources` array to link the new client to protected resources in the same call, with `resourcePrivileges` invoked for each. The `clientPrivileges` callback now receives `clientId` when acting on an existing client, so per-client authorization among users sharing a `clientReference` is possible. Resource identifiers created with `adminCreateOAuthResource` or the `resources` option now follow the same validation as token-request identifiers, rejecting empty-fragment or `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:` schemes. Apps that configure protected resources now keep working when the resource table can't be written at startup; the resources are written on first request instead. The demo app now leaves `Cache-Control` for token responses to the library, keeping them no-store as RFC 6749 §5.1 requires. - Single-use checks (SAML assertions, DPoP proofs, `private_key_jwt` assertions, magic link/OTP verification) now encode their deterministic replay-marker ids to fit the configured id strategy — previously they hit `NOT NULL` errors on SQLite and MySQL with `"uuid"` and accepted replays on Postgres and MongoDB. SIWE sign-in now uses the supplied `email` instead of the wallet-derived address when available. With `generateId: "serial"` these checks still aren't enforced, but Better Auth logs a warning the first time one runs. - Magic link verify no longer double-decodes `callbackURL`, `newUserCallbackURL`, and `errorCallbackURL`, so percent-encoded characters in callback query parameters are preserved. - Password resets and `revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset` changes now revoke sessions and save the new password in one transaction when transactions are enabled, so a failure leaves the old password and sessions in place, and `onPasswordReset` runs after revocation. `/reset-password`, email OTP, and phone number reset no longer spend the link or OTP on a rejected password — it's consumed inside the same transaction as the revocation and write. Phone number password reset now checks the code with the `verifyOTP` option, as `/phone-number/verify` already does. A MongoDB transaction whose commit fails before reaching the server is now aborted instead of staying open until the 60-second timeout. On MongoDB replica sets, concurrent writes that abort with a transient write conflict are now retried for up to 120 seconds instead of failing with 500; `before` database hooks can run again on retry, while `after` hooks run once, after commit. - A sign-up that fails after its session is created no longer leaves that session in secondary storage; the cached copy is written only after the sign-up commits. On adapters without real transactions, writes that can't roll back still run their after-commit hooks before the error is returned. Bulk session lookups now fall back to the database when the cache misses, so device sessions don't disappear after eviction and automatic switching follows the order of held sessions. - SCIM User and Group requests now accept JSON `null` attribute values, such as the unpopulated attributes Microsoft Entra ID sends, instead of returning `400 Bad Request`, attribute names are matched case-insensitively per RFC 7643 — a request that sends the same attribute twice with different letter case returns `400` — and concurrent updates that claim a `userName`, `displayName`, `externalId`, or managed email another request saved first return `409` instead of `500`. `POST /scim/v2/Users` now reprovisions a User that shares an inactive SCIM User's `externalId` in place instead of returning a uniqueness conflict, and D1 concurrent queries on a shared auth instance with Kysely are now allowed. - Async local storage now resolves the native `AsyncLocalStorage` on first use and recognizes a runtime-provided constructor, and an interrupted first initialization no longer hangs subsequent requests. - Adds smoke-test fixtures for the type errors (including `skipLibCheck: false`), plus e2e coverage for password-reset atomicity, D1 concurrency, and SvelteKit 3. Tests for the organization plugin now share fixtures via `beforeAll`, and the release tooling now keeps the title of every PR that adds a changeset. Written for commit 5f4cc5c110fde7f1823e7912378a63f571ff569e. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(email-otp): reuse the existing code when concurrent sends collide

labels.name: core
labels.description: Core infra, API routes, session, cookies, client SDK

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

labels.name: credentials
labels.description: Email/password, magic-link, OTP, phone, username, passkeys

items.body:
Closes #11181

### Problem

On databases that enforce a unique constraint on `verification.identifier` (schemas generated by earlier releases, and many hand-written Prisma/Drizzle schemas), two concurrent `send-verification-otp` requests for the same address both pass `tryReuseOTP` (no row exists yet), both generate a code, and both try to insert. The second insert fails, and `resolveOTP`'s catch handler deleted the first request's row and inserted its own. Both requests still emailed their code, so the user received two emails and the code in the one that arrived first was rejected with `INVALID_OTP`.

This is easy to hit from two devices, and on multi-isolate runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers, where the two requests do not even share a process. It is distinct from #11105, which covers databases *without* a unique constraint (row accumulation and `createdAt` ties); this change only affects the conflict path that runs when the insert is rejected.

### Solution

`resolveOTP` now checks whether a code was already pending before it inserts. When no code was pending and the insert still fails, the row can only belong to a concurrent request, so `resolveOTP` tries to reuse it (`tryReuseOTP`): if it is still alive, has attempts left, and the stored code is recoverable (plain, `encrypted`, or a custom `encrypt`/`decrypt` pair), the second request emails the same code the first request is about to send, so every code the user receives is valid. Reuse on conflict applies regardless of `resendStrategy`, because the point of `rotate` is to invalidate the code a user has already received when they explicitly ask again, not to invalidate a code that is being delivered by a request that started at the same moment. When a code was already pending (a sequential resend), the previous delete-and-recreate runs unchanged, so `resendStrategy: "rotate"` still issues a fresh code and invalidates the old one. Delete-and-recreate also remains the fallback when a concurrent row cannot be reused (hashed storage, expired, attempts exhausted).

No public API changes. Behavior on databases without a unique constraint is unchanged (the insert does not fail there).

### Known limitation

Two *resends* that overlap while a code is already pending still race each other: both rotate, so the later one wins and the earlier email's code is invalid, exactly as with two sequential resends under `rotate`. Closing that window needs an atomic replace at the adapter boundary (the direction of #10443) and is out of scope here.

### Testing

- Added a regression suite that declares a unique index on `verification.identifier` through a plugin schema and sends twice with `Promise.all`: with recoverable storage both `sendVerificationOTP` calls receive the same code, a single row remains, and that code signs in; with hashed storage the last emailed code still signs in (fallback path); a sequential resend under `rotate` still produces a new code and rejects the old one. The first test fails on `main` (`expected '470384' to be '728649'`) and passes with this change.
- `pnpm vitest packages/better-auth/src/plugins/email-otp --run`: 92 passed.
- `pnpm typecheck` passes.

### Breaking changes

None.

items.body: Adds first-class tenant-scoped identity so one Better Auth instance can keep users, accounts, sessions, and verification data isolated per tenant. The same email (and the same OAuth `providerId` + `accountId`) can belong to independent users in different tenants. This is opt-in via [user.identityScope](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/compare/main...WellnessConnect:better-auth:cursor/tenant-scoped-identity-caf6?expand=1#). Existing apps that do not set it are unchanged. Closes #11359 Would be worth treating this as a beta feature while it gets some testing and scope can increase through future PRs like creds caching etc. _Note: I've branched this from `next` and opened against `next` as a base based on what I read in the contributing guidelines. If that needs updating then please let me know :)_ ### Motivation SaaS and multi-tenant consoles often need: - one Better Auth deployment - one database - emails that are unique within a tenant, not globally Today uniqueness and lookups are global ([user.email](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/compare/main...WellnessConnect:better-auth:cursor/tenant-scoped-identity-caf6?expand=1#), [account.providerId](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/compare/main...WellnessConnect:better-auth:cursor/tenant-scoped-identity-caf6?expand=1#) + [account.accountId](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/compare/main...WellnessConnect:better-auth:cursor/tenant-scoped-identity-caf6?expand=1#), verification identifiers, sessions). Workarounds (custom adapters, duplicated instances, hashed emails) leak across APIs and plugins. This change makes the scope part of the auth core. ### API ```typescript export const auth = betterAuth({ user: { additionalFields: { tenantId: { type: "string", required: true, input: false, fieldName: "tenant_id", }, }, identityScope: { field: "tenantId", resolve: ({ headers, request }) => (request?.headers ?? headers)?.get("x-tenant-id"), models: ["passkey", "twoFactor"], }, }, }); ``` - field must name a required, server-owned string user additional field (`type: "string", required: true, input: false`). Clients cannot send it. - `resolve({ headers, request })` returns the current tenant. `null`, `undefined`, or `""` fails. - `models` is optional. Core user, account, session, and verification are always scoped. Use models for plugin tables looked up without a user id (e.g. passkeys, TOTP). After enabling, run `npx auth@latest generate`. Existing installs must backfill the scope column before making it `NOT NULL` and replacing the global email unique constraint. ### Behaviour - Adapter wrapper injects the resolved scope on create and adds it to where-clauses for find/update/delete. - Scope is resolved once per request (cached on the endpoint context). - User email uniqueness becomes composite (`scope, email`). - Account uniqueness becomes composite (`scope, providerId, accountId`). - Sessions and verification rows are tenant-bound; a session token from tenant A does not resolve in tenant B. - Email OTP identifiers are scoped the same way. - Related rows that carry `userId` are checked against a user in the current scope before write. - Schema check still runs against the unwrapped adapter so migrations see the real tables. - `identityScope` is stripped from the user input schema so signup does not require `tenantId` from the client. ### Security Email-verification JWTs were a cross-tenant hole if they only carried email. All internal issuance paths now embed `identityScope`; verify rejects a token whose scope does not match the current request. A verify-email link issued for tenant A cannot confirm the same address in tenant B. ### Limitations Tenant-scoped identity currently requires database-backed sessions and verification. It cannot be combined with `secondaryStorage` or [session.cookieCache](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/compare/main...WellnessConnect:better-auth:cursor/tenant-scoped-identity-caf6?expand=1#). Documented in [docs/content/docs/concepts/database.mdx](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/compare/main...WellnessConnect:better-auth:cursor/tenant-scoped-identity-caf6?expand=1#). This could be added in a follow up. We do not add `tenantId` to every table so RLS is not unlocked by this change. This minimise schema changes and stays focused on achieving the feature requested. ### Out of scope / follow-up - Cookie-cache and secondary-storage session backends - Automatic expand/migrate/contract for existing databases (not sure this is viable and wasn't the way a recent upgrade was done) - Scoping organisations to a single tenant (org-slug remains globally unique). - How this affects the Better Auth infra services. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds tenant-scoped identity so a single Better Auth instance can keep users, accounts, sessions, and verification data isolated per tenant. The same email or OAuth provider account can now map to separate users in different tenants. This is opt-in via `user.identityScope`; apps that don't set it keep today's global identity behavior. - Adds a scoped adapter that injects the resolved scope on create and adds it to all reads, updates, and deletes for scoped models, including plugin credential tables. - Makes email uniqueness composite (`scope` + `email`) and account uniqueness composite (`scope` + `issuer` + `accountId`). Sessions and verification rows only resolve within their tenant, non-unique issuer+accountId lookups are preserved, and operations fail closed when no scope can be resolved. - Binds email-verification tokens to the resolved request scope, including change-email and sign-in flows, so a token from tenant A can't verify the same address in tenant B. - Rejects scope fields that collide with built-in columns or the physical name of one, and points writes against users missing the scope column at backfilling instead of reporting a cross-tenant move. - Requires a database-backed session and verification backend. Rejects `secondaryStorage` and `session.cookieCache`. - Strips the scope from the user input schema so signup never accepts a client-supplied tenant. Jobs and scripts outside an HTTP request resolve a scope through the internal `runWithEndpointContext`, `auth.$context`, and `internalAdapter` APIs, which may change in future releases. **Migration** After enabling, run `npx auth@latest generate`. Existing installs must backfill the scope column before adding the `NOT NULL` constraint and replacing the global unique index. Closes #11359. Written for commit a18294d5bf36cdb096a3fee1e940a4eefa8ff279. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(session): fall back to the database for sessions evicted from secondary storage in findSessions

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

labels.name: locked
labels.description: Locked conversations after being closed for 7 days

items.body: ## Summary With `secondaryStorage` configured as a read-through cache and `session.storeSessionInDatabase: true`, a session evicted from the cache (TTL expiry, memory pressure, restart) silently disappears from `findSessions` results even though it is still valid in the database and `findSession` still resolves it. This restores the batch-read parity that `findSession` (single token) and `listSessions` (per user) already have: tokens missing from the cache are batch-fetched from the database with a single `findMany`, using the same `onlyActiveSessions` clause the non-cached path uses. The exact contract from #9496 for this method is `secondaryStorage batch get → fallback: findMany by token list`; the fallback half was missing. Fixes #11713 ## Root cause In `findSessions` (`packages/better-auth/src/db/internal-adapter.ts`), the `secondaryStorage` branch collected cache hits and returned immediately, ignoring `databaseSessionFallbackEnabled` entirely, while: - `findSession` checks the cache first and falls back to `adapter.findOne` on a miss when `storeSessionInDatabase` is active - `listSessions` queries the database directly under the same flag So the exact session `findSession` returns was absent from `findSessions([token])`. ## What changed - Tokens that resolve from secondary storage are recorded in a `resolvedTokens` set (only on a successful parse; a corrupt cache entry stays unresolved so the database can still rescue it) - When `databaseSessionFallbackEnabled` is false, behavior is unchanged: cache-only deployments keep returning cache-only results, misses stay misses - Otherwise the unresolved (deduplicated) tokens go through one `findMany` with the same `onlyActiveSessions → expiresAt > now` clause as the non-cached path, rows with a missing user join are skipped, and results are pushed through `parseSessionOutput`/`parseUserOutput` exactly like `findSession`'s DB path ## Impact `findSessions` has two in-tree consumers, both in the multi-session plugin, and both are corrected by this: - `/multi-session/list-device-sessions` no longer hides valid device sessions after a cache eviction - the revoke flow no longer wipes every cookie (`deleteSessionCookie`) just because the cache was cold: rotation can still pick the user's other valid session (`findSessions` → `validSessions[0]` → `setSessionCookie`) ## Tests Five regression tests in a new `findSessions database fallback` block, following the existing in-file conventions (`DatabaseSync` + `createStringSecondaryStorage`): 1. cache eviction + `findSession`/`findSessions` parity — the issue's exact scenario 2. partial hit: cached token + evicted token in one call, plus a duplicate input token, asserting no duplicates and both sessions returned 3. corrupt cache entry gets rescued from the database instead of dropped 4. `onlyActiveSessions` honored by the database fallback (expired row excluded, active row returned) — expired row created by flipping `expiresAt` through the raw adapter, since `createSession` clamps `dontRememberMe` 5. cache-only deployment (`storeSessionInDatabase` unset): a cache miss must stay a miss — no DB fallback, pinning the current default behavior Negative control: with the fix reverted, 4 of the 5 new tests fail on current `main` (the cache-only guard is the must-not-regress pin and passes both sides). Full verification: internal-adapter suite 77/77, multi-session plugin suite 10/10, `packages/better-auth/src/plugins` suite green, `packages/better-auth/src/db` green except one pre-existing local Postgres auth failure (`db hooks should preserve a forced UUID on postgres`) that fails identically on pristine `main` without my changes — environment, not code. tsc `--noEmit` clean, biome clean, changeset added. Local note: I tested on Windows; the Postgres test is env-only and unaffected by this change. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `findSessions` silently dropping valid sessions after they are evicted from `secondaryStorage`, restoring parity with `findSession` and `listSessions` when the database is the authoritative session store. Fixes #11713. - Missing tokens are batch-fetched with one `findMany` using the same `onlyActiveSessions` clause as the non-cached path, with a limit set to the missing-token count so the default `findMany` limit can't drop the tail of a large batch. - Results are returned in the caller's input order (deduplicated), preserving multi-session rotation precedence across cache hits and database fallbacks. - Corrupt cache entries — including parseable ones with an invalid `expiresAt` — fall back to the database instead of being dropped; cache-only deployments (`storeSessionInDatabase`) keep returning cache-only results. - `multi-session/list-device-sessions` no longer hides valid sessions after an eviction, and the revoke flow no longer clears cookies when the cache is cold. Written for commit 3682dfbe1edfb8e92086f609e4d09657743370fc. Summary will update on new commits.

  - On SQLite and MySQL, SAML sign-in, DPoP-bound requests checked against the database replay store, `private_key_jwt` client authentication, and magic link or email OTP sign-ins that adopt an unverified account failed with a `NOT NULL` error on the `id` column.   - On Postgres and MongoDB, a reused SAML assertion, DPoP proof, or client assertion was accepted. Each one is now accepted only once.

Better Auth now retries discovery on the next sign-in, callback, or account-linking request for that provider, and the provider works as soon as discovery succeeds. While discovery keeps failing, sign-in and account linking still return `PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND` and callbacks redirect with `error=oauth_provider_not_found`, and each request may wait up to 10 seconds for the retry.

- [#11505](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11505) [`c46992f`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/c46992f6ce548fad0f26f5f07dc8525893e8196c) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Preserve the referenced model and field keys when generating Kysely migrations, so custom table names that match another model key produce the intended foreign keys.

### Patch Changes

- [#11512](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11512) [`4175b34`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/4175b34a8f70d5abb542ac7fc205dc42f564c03a) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Align the installed `@better-auth/utils` version with `better-call` while accepting `^0.4.2 || ^0.5.0` across official package peers.

Before, the adapter passed a JavaScript `Date` to those columns. Drivers such as postgres-js, better-sqlite3 and D1 rejected it, so email sign-up, social sign-in and session refresh failed. Filtering on those columns, for example when listing sessions, failed the same way. Better Auth now writes these dates as UTC text and reads a value without a time zone as UTC.

  If your server's time zone is not UTC and you use node-postgres or mysql2 with a string column that has no time zone, existing rows were written in the server's local time. They now read back shifted by the server's UTC offset, so sessions and verification codes created before the upgrade can expire early or late. Schemas generated by the CLI use date columns and are unaffected.
