- [#11635](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11635) [`a5d582a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/a5d582aaffce1a7457e3da0835a046ba6738c442) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Projects that enable `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` with `skipLibCheck: false` no longer get a TS2430 error from the `@better-auth/mcp` type declarations.

- [#10266](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/10266) [`c68b2cd`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/c68b2cd8a5a03012ea77071ce74a7708210ea5a9) Thanks [@shiminshen](https://github.com/shiminshen)! - Projects that enable `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` can use the `oauthProvider()` and `mcp()` plugins again. Since 1.7.0, adding either plugin to `betterAuth()` failed to type-check with a TS2322 error.

- Updated dependencies [[`4175b34`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/4175b34a8f70d5abb542ac7fc205dc42f564c03a), [`369176e`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/369176e7f6201b4170269991bd3a14d3722eda41), [`6214610`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/62146108c70bbba57aab034bc79f98f016147e78), [`847acd0`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/847acd02bb2d6d17e757ab2b44a837fa0c3ba669), [`c68b2cd`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/c68b2cd8a5a03012ea77071ce74a7708210ea5a9), [`1a9be41`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/1a9be41d184ee2fcbc7f39b1ef1ab5cb492f7147), [`38f3bb3`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/38f3bb34af7de8b17078a5d4e26bf2f430337b58), [`38f3bb3`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/38f3bb34af7de8b17078a5d4e26bf2f430337b58), [`aaf0d7d`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/aaf0d7da3e854ab6e19c184b682308d4f024e4f0)]:
  - @better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.8
## @better-auth/memory-adapter@1.7.8

### Patch Changes

- [#11512](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11512) [`4175b34`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/4175b34a8f70d5abb542ac7fc205dc42f564c03a) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Align the installed `@better-auth/utils` version with `better-call` while accepting `^0.4.2 || ^0.5.0` across official package peers.
## @better-auth/mongo-adapter@1.7.8

### Patch Changes

- [#11512](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11512) [`4175b34`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/4175b34a8f70d5abb542ac7fc205dc42f564c03a) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Align the installed `@better-auth/utils` version with `better-call` while accepting `^0.4.2 || ^0.5.0` across official package peers.

- [#11014](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11014) [`8133265`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/813326536c79291d70897a18b63272fa1e7346a7) Thanks [@codewithbharat](https://github.com/codewithbharat)! - Report the original MongoDB commit failure instead of "Cannot call abortTransaction after calling commitTransaction" during authentication.

- [#11602](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11602) [`ea85d13`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/ea85d133d640233c1564417f3bad611d99356bb9) Thanks [@maxnze1](https://github.com/maxnze1)! - When you pass `client` to `mongodbAdapter`, a transaction whose commit fails before it reaches the server, for example because the commit timed out, is now aborted on the server. Before, the transaction stayed open until MongoDB's `transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds` expired (60 seconds by default), and other writes to the same documents waited or failed with write conflicts. The original commit error is still the one your code receives.

- [#11515](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11515) [`916ef5c`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/916ef5c5307103d9bea44446a40da5d31de2b3fe) Thanks [@BilalAtique](https://github.com/BilalAtique)! - If you pass `client` to `mongodbAdapter` on a replica set, concurrent requests that write the same documents no longer fail with a 500. Before, MongoDB aborted all but one of them with a write conflict, so a SCIM directory that provisions several users at once returned 500 for most of them. The adapter now retries such a transaction, as MongoDB requires, for up to 120 seconds or until your `MongoClient`'s `timeoutMS`. Under contention a request can take longer instead of failing.

  A retry runs the work again. `databaseHooks` `before` hooks can run more than once for one request, and `after` hooks still run once, after the commit. Work that the request does outside the database before it commits can also repeat on a retried request. For example, an email sign-up can send its verification email twice. Requests that succeed on the first attempt are unaffected, and so are other adapters.
## @better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.8

### Patch Changes

- [#11512](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11512) [`4175b34`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/4175b34a8f70d5abb542ac7fc205dc42f564c03a) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Align the installed `@better-auth/utils` version with `better-call` while accepting `^0.4.2 || ^0.5.0` across official package peers.

- [#11625](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11625) [`369176e`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/369176e7f6201b4170269991bd3a14d3722eda41) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Fixed single-use checks for apps that set `advanced.database.generateId: "uuid"`. Default id generation is unaffected, and no migration is needed.
  - On SQLite and MySQL, SAML sign-in, DPoP-bound requests checked against the database replay store, `private_key_jwt` client authentication, and magic link or email OTP sign-ins that adopt an unverified account failed with a `NOT NULL` error on the `id` column. They now work. SIWE sign-in ignored the `email` field and used the wallet-derived address; it now uses the supplied email when no other account has it.
  - On Postgres and MongoDB, a reused SAML assertion, DPoP proof, or client assertion was accepted. Each one is now accepted only once.

  With `generateId: "serial"`, behavior is unchanged: these checks need string ids, and Better Auth now logs a warning the first time one of these flows runs.

- [#10956](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/10956) [`6214610`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/62146108c70bbba57aab034bc79f98f016147e78) Thanks [@disbell](https://github.com/disbell)! - Native OAuth clients and Client ID Metadata Documents can now use custom-scheme redirect URIs with a host and a path, such as Cursor's `cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp/oauth/callback`. Previously, only the authority-free reverse-domain form, such as `com.example.app:/callback`, was accepted, and these registrations failed with `invalid_redirect_uri`.

  Cursor also omits `application_type` when it registers, so the `web` default still rejects it. To accept Cursor, set the new `clientRegistrationDefaultApplicationType` option to `"infer"`. A dynamic registration that omits `application_type` then becomes `native` when any of its redirect URIs uses a custom scheme, and every redirect URI must pass the native rules. Setting `"native"` treats every registration that omits the field as `native`. The default remains `"web"`, and an `application_type` the client sends is never overridden.

  Pairwise clients (`subject_type: "pairwise"`) cannot use these host-bearing custom-scheme redirect URIs. Web clients are unaffected: they still accept only `https` redirect URIs on non-loopback hosts.

- [#11658](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11658) [`847acd0`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/847acd02bb2d6d17e757ab2b44a837fa0c3ba669) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - If you configure `clientPrivileges`, the callback now receives `clientId` when a user reads, updates, deletes, rotates the secret of, or configures scopes on an existing client. You can use it to allow or deny actions per client among users who share a `clientReference`. Before, the callback could not tell which client the request targeted. `clientId` is absent for creating and listing clients, and the callback still cannot grant access to a client owned by someone else, apart from the existing scope-only updates through `adminUpdateOAuthClient`. Existing callbacks keep working unchanged.

- [#10266](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/10266) [`c68b2cd`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/c68b2cd8a5a03012ea77071ce74a7708210ea5a9) Thanks [@shiminshen](https://github.com/shiminshen)! - Projects that enable `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` can use the `oauthProvider()` and `mcp()` plugins again. Since 1.7.0, adding either plugin to `betterAuth()` failed to type-check with a TS2322 error.

- [#11654](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11654) [`1a9be41`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/1a9be41d184ee2fcbc7f39b1ef1ab5cb492f7147) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Authorized client owners can pause and resume an OAuth client by updating its `disabled` field through `adminUpdateOAuthClient`. A disabled client cannot obtain new tokens, and token introspection reports its existing tokens as inactive.

- [#11655](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11655) [`38f3bb3`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/38f3bb34af7de8b17078a5d4e26bf2f430337b58) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - If you register OAuth clients from your server with `adminCreateOAuthClient`, you can now pass `resources` to link the new client to protected resources in the same call. Previously you created the client first and then called `adminLinkClientResource` for each resource. When `resourcePrivileges` is configured, it is called with the `link` action for each requested resource, and a missing or disabled resource rejects the registration with `invalid_target`. Dynamic client registration and `adminLinkClientResource` are unchanged.

- [#11655](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11655) [`38f3bb3`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/38f3bb34af7de8b17078a5d4e26bf2f430337b58) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Resource identifiers created with `adminCreateOAuthResource` or listed in the `resources` option now follow the same rules as the `resource` parameter in token and registration requests. An identifier with an empty fragment (`https://api.example.com/#`) or a `javascript:`, `data:`, or `vbscript:` scheme is rejected, and startup seeding skips it with a warning. Token requests already rejected these identifiers, so no working resource is affected. Setups with a custom `identifierValidator` are unaffected.

- [#11726](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11726) [`aaf0d7d`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/aaf0d7da3e854ab6e19c184b682308d4f024e4f0) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Apps that configure protected resources, through `resources` in `oauthProvider()` or `resource` in `mcp()`, keep working when the resource table cannot be written at startup. Since 1.7.0, a database that was briefly unreachable, a table that was not migrated yet, or two instances starting at the same time made every auth route fail until the process restarted, and `auth generate` failed for Drizzle projects. The auth instance now starts, logs the error through your configured `logger`, and writes the resources on the first request that needs one.

  With Prisma on PostgreSQL, CockroachDB, or MongoDB, a resource without `allowedScopes`, including the one `mcp()` adds, still cannot be stored. The app now starts, but requests that use any configured resource fail until you declare `allowedScopes` for that resource.
## @better-auth/passkey@1.7.8

### Patch Changes

- [#11512](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11512) [`4175b34`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/4175b34a8f70d5abb542ac7fc205dc42f564c03a) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Align the installed `@better-auth/utils` version with `better-call` while accepting `^0.4.2 || ^0.5.0` across official package peers.

### Patch Changes

- [#11512](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11512) [`4175b34`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/4175b34a8f70d5abb542ac7fc205dc42f564c03a) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Align the installed `@better-auth/utils` version with `better-call` while accepting `^0.4.2 || ^0.5.0` across official package peers.
## @better-auth/scim@1.7.8

### Patch Changes

- [#11512](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11512) [`4175b34`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/4175b34a8f70d5abb542ac7fc205dc42f564c03a) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Align the installed `@better-auth/utils` version with `better-call` while accepting `^0.4.2 || ^0.5.0` across official package peers.

- [#11644](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11644) [`f556970`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f556970135281ea6d2827b0b09154c5011c5d0e3) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - If your SCIM provider sends attribute names with different letter case than the SCIM schema, such as `Active` or `Emails`, Better Auth now applies them. Previously these keys were ignored while the request still succeeded, so a `PUT` with `Active: false` left the User active. A request that sends the same attribute twice with different letter case now returns `400 Bad Request`. Providers that send the standard attribute names are unaffected.

- [#11638](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11638) [`39f0980`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/39f09800b7cf62d1e01b0461a35bb79fcd90f3e0) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - SCIM User and Group requests now accept JSON `null` attribute values, such as the unpopulated attributes Microsoft Entra ID sends, instead of returning `400 Bad Request`. In `POST` and `PUT` bodies a `null` attribute is treated as omitted, and in PATCH a `null` value removes the attribute. `active: null` is still rejected, and `null` on a read-only attribute is ignored.

- [#11167](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11167) [`666e1de`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/666e1def9796bcdd2f0646f4b7223798a947fd2d) Thanks [@jonathansamines](https://github.com/jonathansamines)! - Fix `POST /scim/v2/Users` rejecting a reprovisioned user with a uniqueness conflict when an inactive SCIM User already has the same `externalId`, such as when Okta reassigns a deactivated user. The inactive SCIM User is now reprovisioned in place and keeps its ID and linked Better Auth User.

- [#11669](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11669) [`8409fb2`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/8409fb250d30fdd54585a3593ef86fb5e59f065b) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - SCIM directories that send concurrent updates now get a `409` uniqueness error when a User `PATCH`, Group `PUT`, or Group `PATCH` claims a `userName`, `displayName`, `externalId`, or managed email that another request saved first. Previously the losing request failed with a `500` server error. Requests that don't race are unaffected.
## @better-auth/sso@1.7.8

### Patch Changes

- [#11512](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11512) [`4175b34`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/4175b34a8f70d5abb542ac7fc205dc42f564c03a) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Align the installed `@better-auth/utils` version with `better-call` while accepting `^0.4.2 || ^0.5.0` across official package peers.

- [#11378](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11378) [`6c89bb1`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/6c89bb18f191a9f6cf7ce893b4af1c329cd4104d) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Updating an SSO provider with a partial `mapping` no longer fails validation. Since v1.7.0, `updateSSOProvider` rejected any OIDC or SAML mapping that left out `email` or `name`, even though both have documented defaults and v1.6 accepted them. `registerSSOProvider` now accepts these mappings too. Omitted fields fall back to the defaults. A mapping that passes `id` is still rejected, as described in the v1.7 upgrade guide.

- [#11438](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11438) [`61f64f4`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/61f64f46adacc1c7c1053aa62e4f6b83619ccb61) Thanks [@Tushar-Khandelwal-2004](https://github.com/Tushar-Khandelwal-2004)! - Reject OIDC SSO provider registration when the configured issuer differs from the discovery document, including trailing slash mismatches, instead of failing later during sign-in. Existing providers with a mismatched issuer are unchanged and must be reconfigured to match the discovery document.

- [#11640](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11640) [`a878f9a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/a878f9ab47e896a106a449f043f0149b20728851) Thanks [@Sandipxg](https://github.com/Sandipxg)! - OIDC providers that send the email claim as a list of addresses, such as Azure AD B2C's `emails`, can now sign users in. Previously the callback failed with `missing_user_info`, even with `mapping: { email: "emails" }`. Better Auth now uses the first address in the list. Providers that send `emails` instead of `email` need `mapping: { email: "emails" }`.

- [#11743](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11743) [`adbdc06`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/adbdc06e339b8726803f21f9bcb695205d5081c6) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - SAML providers that already have linked accounts can change `samlConfig.callbackUrl`, their post-login redirect, again. Since 1.7.0, that update returned 409 `Cannot change SSO provider identity fields while linked accounts exist`, because the redirect was still treated as the 1.6 Assertion Consumer Service URL. `guardProviderMutation` now reports a `callbackUrl`-only change with `isAuthenticationBoundaryChange: false`.

- [#11687](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11687) [`182e92b`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/182e92bd8a6d101fee6430cf968f823e6cd044bd) Thanks [@kaiizer777](https://github.com/kaiizer777)! - SAML providers that already have linked accounts can rotate their IdP signing certificate again. Since 1.7.0, changing `cert` or `idpMetadata.cert` through `updateSSOProvider` returned 409 `Cannot change SSO provider identity fields while linked accounts exist`, so the only way to rotate was to delete the provider, which also removed its account links and domain verification. `guardProviderMutation` still receives certificate changes as authentication-boundary changes, so a guard that rejects those keeps blocking them.

### Patch Changes

- [#9684](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/9684) [`72a6394`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/72a6394e30ced6654ebffe3c5b74dc1b570f6880) Thanks [@nikhilgupta58](https://github.com/nikhilgupta58)! - Stop logging a "Stripe webhook failed" error when a one-time `payment` mode checkout session completes.

# Releases
## better-auth@1.8.0-beta.0

### Minor Changes

- [#11751](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11751) [`5fd850f`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/5fd850f926a9500219d14d13adc5cbd2436d105e) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - On every database adapter, the verification email for an email sign-up, or for a new social or SSO account, is now sent only after the account is saved, and `onExistingUserSignUp` runs after the sign-up request's database work completes. A sign-up that rolls back, or that MongoDB runs again after a write conflict, no longer sends an extra email or an email for an account that doesn't exist.

  Check your setup for two changes:
  - If `sendVerificationEmail` or `onExistingUserSignUp` throws during a sign-up, the sign-up now succeeds and the error is logged. Before, a callback that threw synchronously failed the sign-up and rolled it back. To reject a sign-up, use a `databaseHooks.user.create.before` hook.
  - If a `databaseHooks` `user` or `account` `after` hook throws during a sign-up, the request still fails, but the verification email is no longer sent. The user can request a new one.

  With `secondaryStorage` and `session.storeSessionInDatabase: true`, social, SSO, one-tap and oauth-proxy sign-ins now cache their session after the commit, as email sign-up already did. A failed cache write is logged instead of failing the sign-in. This doesn't apply when `session.preserveSessionInDatabase` is `true`, where a failed cache write still fails the sign-in.

- [#11772](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11772) [`ec0afde`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/ec0afdef5aa6d0dfb93b14357ae470977e28ecdf) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - When the same device code is approved and denied at the same time, for example from two open approval pages, only the first decision now takes effect, and the other request fails with `invalid_request` and "Device code already processed". Previously, both requests reported success and the later one replaced the first, so a denied device could still receive tokens.

  The `/device/approve` error type no longer lists `device_code_already_processed`. The server never returned that code; an already decided code has always returned `invalid_request`. TypeScript code that compares against `device_code_already_processed` must check `invalid_request` instead.

- [#11610](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11610) [`034da07`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/034da07dbe92a0ce0ef735f2f31baff756cc25d1) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - If you wrote a custom `DeviceAuthorizationGrant`, rename `assertSessionRedemption` to `assertStandaloneUse`. It now also runs for `/device`, `/device/approve`, and `/device/deny`, and receives `use: "redeem"` or `use: "approve"`. `getVerificationContext`, `verificationOpenAPIProperties`, and the interface's second type parameter were removed, because `/device` no longer returns grant details. A grant that approves codes on its own pages can use the newly exported `findDeviceCodeByUserCode`, `assertDeviceCodePending`, `decideDeviceCode`, and `buildVerificationUris`. Apps that use `deviceAuthorization()` or `oauthDeviceAuthorization()` without a custom grant are unaffected.

### Patch Changes

- [#11772](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11772) [`ec0afde`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/ec0afdef5aa6d0dfb93b14357ae470977e28ecdf) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Device clients that poll `/device/token` or `/oauth2/token` too soon after their device code expires now receive `expired_token` right away. Previously they received `slow_down` and learned that the code had expired only on a later poll.

- Updated dependencies []:
  - @better-auth/core@1.8.0-beta.0
  - @better-auth/drizzle-adapter@1.8.0-beta.0
  - @better-auth/kysely-adapter@1.8.0-beta.0
  - @better-auth/memory-adapter@1.8.0-beta.0
  - @better-auth/mongo-adapter@1.8.0-beta.0
  - @better-auth/prisma-adapter@1.8.0-beta.0
  - @better-auth/telemetry@1.8.0-beta.0
## @better-auth/ciba@1.8.0-beta.0

### Minor Changes

- [#11785](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11785) [`25f7617`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/25f7617db6628059370da0280f1ce68fd2d92f1c) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Add `@better-auth/ciba`, OpenID Connect Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication (CIBA) for `oauthProvider()`. A client that knows who it is acting for, such as an AI agent or a support tool, asks for a user by `login_hint` at `/oauth2/bc-authorize`. Your `sendNotification` callback sends that user a link, the user approves or denies on your existing sign-in and consent pages, and the client collects tokens at `/oauth2/token`, either by polling or after the server calls it back (`deliveryModes: ["poll", "ping"]`).

  Consent is always shown, only the user the client named can decide, and your consent page receives the client's `binding_message` to display. Clients register `backchannel_token_delivery_mode`, and for ping `backchannel_client_notification_endpoint`, through dynamic registration, a client metadata document, or admin client creation, and registration rejects unsupported values. Public clients such as agents can take part with `allowPublicClients`; they send `client_id` in the form body and should bind their tokens with DPoP. `resolveUser` receives the requesting client, so with open registration you can accept only identifiers that client was already given.

  The plugin adds a `cibaRequest` table. Run `npx auth@latest migrate` with the built-in Kysely adapter, or run `npx auth@latest generate` and apply the schema with your ORM.

The call refuses a decision for any user other than the one the client named, and approved scopes must stay within the request and include `openid`. You can also pass the `authTime`, `acr`, and `amr` your app established, and they are issued in the ID token. A ping client is called back as it is after a decision from the link.

## @better-auth/oauth-provider@1.8.0-beta.0

### Minor Changes

- [#11610](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11610) [`034da07`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/034da07dbe92a0ce0ef735f2f31baff756cc25d1) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - If you use `oauthDeviceAuthorization()`, users now approve OAuth device codes on the provider's sign-in, account selection, post-login, and consent pages, the same as an authorization request. Your device verification page sends the browser to `/oauth2/authorize?user_code=<code>`. The consent page always opens for a device and receives `user_code` to display, and afterwards the user returns to your verification page with `status=approved` or `status=denied`, or with `error` and `error_description` when the code is unknown, expired, or already used. Device tokens and their refreshes now carry the `referenceId` from `postLogin.consentReferenceId` and the user's authentication time, and each approval records a consent.

  Previously, approval pages called `/device/approve` or `/device/deny` directly, which skipped post-login selection and consent. Those endpoints and `/device` now refuse OAuth device codes with `invalid_request` and name the URL to use, so update your approval page before upgrading. Standalone `deviceAuthorization()` setups are unaffected.

  `oauthDeviceAuthorization()` adds optional `referenceId` and `authTime` columns to the `deviceCode` table. Apply them before deploying: run `npx auth@latest migrate` with the built-in Kysely adapter, or run `npx auth@latest generate` and apply the schema with your ORM.

- [#11826](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11826) [`296133c`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/296133cc414ac24283ed8e33501e2e4e501ab5e0) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Device authorization and CIBA clients that poll the token endpoint with a missing or invalid DPoP proof now receive `invalid_dpop_proof` and can poll again with a valid proof. Previously the rejected poll used up the approved device code or CIBA request, so the user had to approve again. Clients that send valid proofs, or no proof when none is required, are unaffected.

  Extension grants that consume a one-time credential can call `provider.resolveConfirmation()` before the claim and pass its result to `issueTokens` as `confirmation` to get the same behavior.

- [#11788](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11788) [`cd404a0`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/cd404a0b46abb929ccaea0129ecdff23fb074a8f) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - With `oauthDeviceAuthorization()` and an `authenticationContext` resolver, ID tokens from the device code grant now carry the `acr` and `amr` that `resolve` returns when the user approves the device code, and refreshed ID tokens keep them. Previously device-issued ID tokens always reported `acr: "0"` and no `amr`. Setups without `oauthDeviceAuthorization()` are unaffected.

  This adds optional `acr` and `amr` columns to the `deviceCode` table when `oauthDeviceAuthorization()` is enabled. Apply them before deploying: run `npx auth@latest migrate` with the built-in Kysely adapter, or run `npx auth@latest generate` and apply the schema with your ORM.

- [#11787](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11787) [`ed71a21`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/ed71a211e803f9f336ebfa83c4ef96610e621fd1) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - `oauthProvider()` accepts a new `authenticationContext` option that sets the `acr` and `amr` claims in ID tokens. List the classes you issue in `acrValuesSupported`, which discovery advertises as `acr_values_supported`, and return the current session's `acr` and `amr` from `resolve`. Previously every ID token carried `acr: "0"` and no `amr`, and that is still the default.

  With a resolver, a request whose essential `claims.id_token.acr` the session does not satisfy fails with `access_denied`. A voluntary request through `acr_values` continues and the ID token reports the session's current `acr`. A resolver that returns an `acr` outside `acrValuesSupported`, or an `amr` that is not a string array, fails the authorization with `server_error`. ID tokens from refreshed tokens keep the `acr` and `amr` of the original authorization.

  This release adds optional `acr` and `amr` columns to the `oauthRefreshToken` table, which every `oauthProvider()` setup needs. Apply them before deploying: run `npx auth@latest migrate` with the built-in Kysely adapter, or run `npx auth@latest generate` and apply the schema with your ORM.

- [#11767](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11767) [`2417879`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/2417879cf6b2cb5c97ab679b83df0038760e045d) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Plugins that extend `oauthProvider()` with `extendOAuthProvider()` can now define their own client registration fields with `clientMetadata`. A client with invalid values for those fields is rejected with `invalid_client_metadata` when it registers through `/oauth2/register` or a client metadata document, or when an admin creates or updates it, instead of when it first uses them.

  Dynamic registration and client metadata documents now accept the fields an extension declares as top-level fields and store them in the client's `metadata`. They still ignore all other unrecognized fields. Registration in setups without such an extension is unchanged.

  Updating a client with an empty `metadata` object now clears its stored metadata. Previously the update left the old metadata in place.

- [#9923](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/9923) [`c750fc5`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/c750fc5ad2cccf42d3bc6de9820c510a8cdb2cd4) Thanks [@shiminshen](https://github.com/shiminshen)! - OAuth providers can now notify relying parties through the browser with OpenID Connect Front-Channel Logout 1.0. Register a `frontchannel_logout_uri` on a client, using the scheme, host, and port of one of its `redirect_uris`. When a user logs out through `/oauth2/end-session` in the browser, the provider loads that URI in a hidden iframe with `iss` and `sid`, then continues to the verified `post_logout_redirect_uri`. Clients with this URI also receive `sid` in their ID tokens.

  Front-channel logout is reliable only when the provider and its relying parties share a registrable domain, because browsers block or partition third-party cookies. Use back-channel logout for relying parties on other sites. Providers with no front-channel clients see no change.

  Run `npx auth@latest migrate`, or `npx auth@latest generate` if you manage the schema yourself, to add the `frontchannelLogoutUri` and `frontchannelLogoutSessionRequired` columns to `oauthClient`.

- [#11610](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11610) [`034da07`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/034da07dbe92a0ce0ef735f2f31baff756cc25d1) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Plugins that extend OAuth Provider through `extendOAuthProvider()` can register `interactionRequests`: requests other than an authorization request, keyed by a query parameter, that users approve on the provider's sign-in, account selection, post-login, and consent pages. The provider resumes them through `/oauth2/authorize`, can require consent on every approval, and sends errors to a page the request names. `oauthDeviceAuthorization()` uses one keyed by `user_code`.

- [#11796](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11796) [`9f53222`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/9f532221bee7cd99a5c4e6593313dead87bf8f0d) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - `/oauth2/revoke` and `/oauth2/introspect` now follow RFC 7009 and RFC 7662 when they look up the presented token. Check your clients and tests for these changes:
  - `/oauth2/revoke` returns `200` for an unknown or already revoked token. Before, it returned `400 invalid_request`, including for a second revoke of the same refresh token and for a revoke that raced a refresh.
  - A token sent with the wrong `token_type_hint` is found. Before, `/oauth2/revoke` returned `400` and left the token active, and `/oauth2/introspect` reported `{ "active": false }` for a valid token.
  - Revoking a token issued to a different client returns `400 invalid_request` when the caller is a confidential client. Before, it returned `200` without revoking anything, or `400 unsupported_token_type` for a JWT access token. A public client gets `200`, and the token stays valid.
  - A JWT-shaped token that fails verification (for example `alg: none`, a forged signature, or an unknown `kid`) is treated as an invalid token: `200` from revoke, `{ "active": false }` from introspect, and `401 invalid_token` from userinfo. Before, all three returned `500`.
  - At `/oauth2/token`, a refresh token without the configured `prefix.refreshToken` now gets `400 invalid_grant`, like any other unknown refresh token. Before, it got `400 invalid_token`.
  - An async `formatRefreshToken.encrypt`, such as the JWE example in the docs, now works. Before, the issued refresh token was the string `[object Promise]`.
  - In an extension grant handler, `provider.validateAccessToken` returns `{ active: false }` for an unknown token instead of throwing. `provider.requireActiveAccessToken` still throws.

  A valid JWT access token still returns `400 unsupported_token_type` from revoke, and failed client authentication still returns `401`.

- [#11763](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11763) [`c7c8331`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/c7c83314009540df912fb608b746fad3c02214ee) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - If you set a `reference_id` claim on access tokens yourself, through `customAccessTokenClaims`, an extension, or a resource's `customClaims`, it is now dropped with a warning, because the provider sets this claim itself. Rename your claim to keep sending it. When `postLogin.consentReferenceId` returns a consent reference, such as an organization, JWT access tokens now include it as `reference_id`, and introspection returns it. Setups that use neither see no change to their tokens.

  Services that receive a user's access token, such as an MCP server or a backend for frontend, can now exchange it for an access token to another registered API with OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693), instead of forwarding the user's token. Add `oauthTokenExchange()` next to `oauthProvider()` and register the service as a confidential client with the `TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` grant. The exchanged token represents the same user and keeps the consent reference, such as the organization, the user approved. It is limited to the subject token's scopes and never outlives the subject token. Delegation (`actor_token`) and refresh tokens for exchanged tokens are not supported yet.

  Extension authors can pass `maxExpiresAt` to `issueTokens` to cap when the access token expires.

- [#11746](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11746) [`0d4609f`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/0d4609f4a904d919353acae7ef04d2e68ff1be15) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - The `/oauth2/token`, `/oauth2/introspect`, and `/oauth2/revoke` endpoints now reject form parameters sent more than once with `400 invalid_request`, and the description names the parameter. For example, `code=a&code=b` at the token endpoint, for any grant type, returns "code must not be repeated", and `token=a&token=b` at introspection returns "token must not be repeated". Before, these endpoints used the last value, so the token endpoint could issue tokens and introspection or revocation acted on a token other than the first one sent. At the token endpoint, `resource` and `audience` may still repeat, and extension grants now receive every `audience` value instead of only the last one. A parameter sent without a value counts as omitted wherever it appears, so `scope=read&scope=` is the same as `scope=read`. Clients that send each parameter once and never send an empty value are unaffected.

  A malformed `resource` at the token endpoint, such as one with a fragment or a relative URI, now returns `invalid_target` instead of `invalid_request`. If your client matches on the error code for these requests, update it. An empty `resource` is now treated as omitted, as RFC 6749 §3.2 requires; before, `resource=` returned `invalid_request`.

  Token, introspection, registration, and end-session requests rejected by schema validation, such as a missing `grant_type`, now carry `Cache-Control: no-store`, like every other response from those endpoints.

- [#11650](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11650) [`6e5a88e`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/6e5a88e57b0b5253bc49797cede415ff27a82931) Thanks [@gustavovalverde](https://github.com/gustavovalverde)! - Pairwise clients with authority-free private-use redirect URIs, such as `com.example.app:/callback`, or loopback redirect URIs, such as `http://localhost:8787/callback`, now each receive a `sub` of their own. Previously, unrelated clients of either kind could receive the same pairwise `sub`. HTTPS clients on the same host still share a `sub`.

  This adds a `sectorIdentifier` column to the `oauthClient` table. Run `npx auth@latest migrate`, or `npx auth@latest generate` for your ORM, before upgrading. Existing clients keep their current `sub`; the new rule applies to clients created after the upgrade.

items.title: fix(oauth-provider): stop writing configured resources during init
items.body:
### What
Fixes #11725 (Part 2) by eliminating all database I/O and row writes during `betterAuth()` construction with configured `resources` or `mcp({ resource })`.

### Why
Previously, constructing `betterAuth()` with configured resources eagerly called `seedResourcesOnce` during plugin initialization. This caused:
- Eager database operations (`oauthResource.findOne` + `create`) during module import/startup.
- Blocked context resolution during `next build`, `auth generate`, and unit tests that never use OAuth.
- Writes to production databases with build/CLI credentials.
- Reliance on error-string matching (`MISSING_TABLE_PATTERN`) and post-insert re-reads to survive unmigrated databases or concurrent boots.
- A second lazy seed call inside `getResource` on the first token/authorization read.

### Implementation Details
1. **Zero-I/O In-Memory Indexing**: Configured resources are normalized and indexed synchronously in memory (`indexConfiguredResources`) into a per-options `WeakMap` during plugin creation with zero database queries.
2. **Read-Time Resource Combine**:
   - `combineResource` synchronously combines persisted database rows with in-memory configured entries per `resourceSeedMode`:
     - `insertOnly` (default): database row wins once it exists; configured entry used if no row.
     - `merge`: present configured fields override row values; omitted fields preserve row values.
     - `overwrite`: configured values replace row values while preserving persistent row identity (`id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `policyVersion`).
   - `getResource` reads only stored rows and combines config post-lookup.
   - `getResourceCustomClaims` resolves config-only entries alongside stored rows using a single `findMany` query.
   - Admin `listResourcesEndpoint` concatenates stored rows with unpersisted configured entries (`getConfiguredResourcesWithoutRows`).
3. **Lazy, Idempotent Row Creation**:
   - Implemented `ensureResourceRow` with an in-process single-flight lock (`withResourceInsertLock`) and unique-constraint race recovery (re-reading the winner row if a concurrent process inserts first).
   - Rows are created only when an external foreign key needs one (before writing `oauthClientResource` links during client registration or admin link endpoints) or when an admin updates a row-less configured resource.
4. **Complete Seed Machinery Removal**:
   - Removed init seed hook, `seedResources`, `seedResourcesOnce`, `SeedState`, `seedStates`, `getSeedState`, `resetSeedStateForTests`, `logStartupSeedFailure`, `buildSeedUpdate`, `MISSING_TABLE_PATTERN`, and the lazy seed inside `getResource`.
   - Removed all Part 2 markers (`TODO(#11725)`) while preserving all Part 1 markers (`FIXME(#11725)`) intact.
5. **Documentation & Changeset**:
   - Updated `oauth-provider.mdx` and `mcp.mdx` to reflect in-memory configuration and lazy row creation.
   - Added minor changeset `.changeset/lazy-oauth-resource-rows.md` targeting `@better-auth/oauth-provider`.

### Verification
- 8 hermetic test suites passed (291/291 tests green):
  - Zero-I/O construction verified (`resource-startup.test.ts`: 0 adapter calls and 0 rows created).
  - Config-only token issuance, policy enforcement, and custom claims introspection verified.
  - Concurrent dynamic client registration single-row creation verified (`register.test.ts`).
  - Read-time mode matrix (`insertOnly`, `merge`, `overwrite`) verified (`resources.test.ts`).
  - Admin CRUD on row-less configured resources verified (`oauthResource/endpoints.test.ts`).
  - Memoized deferred identifier validation on read verified.
- `pnpm --filter @better-auth/oauth-provider typecheck`: Clean (Exit 0).
- `pnpm biome check`: Clean (Exit 0).
- Build output (`tsdown`): Clean (Exit 0).
- Exact 1 commit, exactly 17 authorized files, zero core schema/DDL modifications.

items.body:
Fixes #10856

## Root cause

`VerifyAccessTokenOptions.jwksUrl` was typed `string` from the plugin's first commit (`686fba4e1`) and was never widened. The in-process JWKS source was added later, in `734328414` (#9987), which introduced `jwksFetch: string | (() => Promise<JSONWebKeySet | undefined>)` plus `jwksCacheKey` on the internal `JwksFetchOptions` type — and converted `introspect.ts` and `revoke.ts` to use it. It did not touch `verifyAccessTokenPayload` or the public `jwksUrl` field.

The result was a split contract:

| surface | JWKS source | cache key |
|---|---|---|
| resource server | `jwksUrl?: string` | none — dropped at the call site |
| introspection | url or in-process closure | `jwksCacheKey: jwtPlugin` |
| revocation | url or in-process closure | `jwksCacheKey: jwtPlugin` |

A resource server co-located with the authorization server therefore had to make an HTTP request to *its own* `/jwks` endpoint for a key set already present in the process. The cache key was also never forwarded, so even a function source would have been re-read on every verification.

### Security defect found in review and fixed in this PR

The first commit of this PR introduced an exploitable cross-issuer flaw, which the second commit fixes. The function-source cache was `WeakMap<object, JwksCacheEntry>`, keyed only by the caller's `jwksCacheKey` object, with no issuer dimension. A resource server trusting two issuers that shared one `jwksCacheKey` cached the first issuer's key set and then verified tokens against it on the second issuer's path: a token **signed with the first issuer's private key but claiming the second issuer's `iss` and `aud`** was accepted, and the second issuer's resolver was never called. The `kid` freshness check treated the cached set as valid because the token's `kid` was present in it.

`iss` and `aud` enforcement does not prevent this. Those checks constrain claims the attacker already fully controls, because the attacker holds the signing key and signs whatever payload they write. The property that binds a token to an issuer is *which key verifies its signature*, and the cache reused the wrong one. It is the same confusion as handing the verifier a union of both issuers' keys, reachable by accident.

## What changed

Second commit (the security fix):
- `packages/core/src/oauth2/verify.ts` — the function-source cache is now `WeakMap<object, Map<string, JwksCacheEntry>>`. The outer key is still the caller's object, so entries are released with it and a per-request key still cannot accumulate. The inner key is a slot for the trusted issuer set, threaded down from `opts.verifyOptions.issuer` inside `verifyJwsAccessToken`. The slot is `JSON.stringify` of the sorted, de-duplicated issuer array behind a prefix that keeps it distinct from the reserved no-issuer slot, so distinct issuer sets can never collide. An issuer mismatch is treated as a **cache miss**, so the resolver is called and the verified issuer gets its own entry — rejecting instead would turn a shared key into a hard failure that reads as an outage. Callers that configure no issuer (`getJwks` → `introspect.ts`, `revoke.ts`, `logout.ts`) keep a reserved slot and behave exactly as before. String sources are untouched, since they are already cached per url.

First commit (the original feature):
- `packages/core/src/oauth2/verify.ts` — widened `jwksUrl` to the union the internal `JwksFetchOptions.jwksFetch` already uses, via indexed access so the union has exactly one declaration and no new exported name. Added `jwksCacheKey` and forwarded it into the existing `verifyJwsAccessToken` call.
- `packages/oauth-provider/src/client-resource.ts` — mirrored the shape on the `oauthProviderResourceClient` actions. Where `jwksUrl` is *required*, `NonNullable<...>` is used so it still rejects `undefined` exactly as `jwksUrl: string` did.
- Tests, docs, changeset.

## Why this is minimal

`string` is a strict subset of the widened union, so the feature half is a pure widening: every existing caller keeps compiling and behaves identically.

- `getJwksForVerification`'s string branch never reads `jwksCacheKey`, and the string cache is still keyed by url.
- `resolveVerifyAccessTokenOptions`'s default `??` chain is byte-for-byte identical to `main`.
- `introspect.ts`, `revoke.ts` and `logout.ts` are not modified.
- No endpoint metadata, DB schema, migration, middleware, rate limit, error code, or error status is touched. `verifyOptions` handling is untouched — introspection still deliberately omits jose's `audience` and validates `aud` against the resource model, while the resource-server path still requires `audience`.
- `packages/mcp/**` is deliberately untouched.
- The public API surface does not grow: no new export in `core/src/oauth2/index.ts`, and the cache helpers are module-private.

## Correctness and security

- **Cross-issuer substitution is closed.** A cached key set is only reused for the issuer set it was read for.
- **Fail-closed is preserved.** A key set that does not contain the token's `kid` still yields `UNAUTHORIZED` / `401`.
- **No attacker-reachable surface.** `jwksUrl`, `jwksCacheKey` and the issuer used to scope the cache all come from server configuration. None is read from a request body, query parameter, header, cookie, or token claim.
- **No new SSRF/redirect surface.** The function path performs no fetch at all; the string path and its redirect refusal are untouched.
- **No key leakage.** The cache is a `WeakMap`, so entries are released with the caller's key object and cannot accumulate across tenants.
- **Sharing one `jwksCacheKey` across issuers and audiences is now safe** — each issuer set gets its own entry. The only remaining footgun is performance: with no `jwksCacheKey`, a function source is read on every verification.

### Honest residuals
- A configured `issuer` **list** (`issuer: [A, B]`) is one trust set and therefore one cache entry, so a token signed by A's key claiming `iss: B` verifies. That is jose's own list semantics, it is already true for a string source on `main`, and per-issuer slots for list members would break the legitimate multi-issuer case. The correct configuration is one issuer per verification.
- The no-issuer slot used by `getJwks` callers is shared. Those callers run inside the authorization server against its own plugin instance and are single-issuer in practice.
- There is no anti-stampede cooldown on the function-source path. That is pre-existing and identical for string sources.

## How it was verified

**The bypass, red → green.** With the fix reverted, a token signed by issuer A's key claiming `iss: B` / `aud: B` resolved successfully on the B verification path. After the fix it is rejected with `invalid access token`, and B's resolver is called. 3 of the new tests fail on the reverted code.

**Cache forwarding, red → green.** Removing the single forwarded property makes the resolver read 3 times instead of 1:
```
FAIL  verify.test.ts > … > should read an in-process jwks source once across verifications sharing a jwksCacheKey
AssertionError: expected 3 to be 1
FAIL  client-resource.test.ts > … > should read the in-process jwks source once across verifications sharing a jwksCacheKey
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 3 times
```

**Type red → green.** Reverting the `jwksUrl` declarations to `string` produces 5 compile errors in `@better-auth/core` and 4 in `@better-auth/oauth-provider`.

**18 bypass variants attempted against the fix, all rejected:** the original forgery on both `verifyBearerToken` and `verifyAccessTokenRequest`; 12 interleaved warm/attack orderings in both directions; 8 rounds of concurrent first-writes on a fresh cache key; the no-`kid` `forceRefresh` retry path; the reserved-slot boundary against 25 issuer values; and 50 verifications carrying 25 distinct attacker-chosen `iss` values, which produced 1 resolver read. Concurrent first-writes can drop an entry, which is a miss and therefore fail-safe.

**Green:** `verify.test.ts` 53/53, `client-resource.test.ts` 5/5, `@better-auth/core`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider` and `@better-auth/mcp` 1717/1717 across 97 files. `pnpm typecheck` exit 0. `biome check --error-on-warnings`, `format:check`, `lint:spell` all exit 0. Tests are deterministic and shuffle-order independent: no sleeps, no real clock, no network.

The tests that pass without the fix are guards, not proofs — they pin the documented uncached default, the `remoteVerify.force` short-circuit, the fail-closed `kid`-mismatch case, and that string sources and the no-issuer `getJwks` path are unchanged.

## Notes for reviewers

- **`packages/oauth-provider` tests resolve `@better-auth/core` from `dist`, not `src`.** Vitest externalizes the workspace `better-auth` dependency, so `dev-source` does not apply to package projects. `turbo.json` gives `test` a `dependsOn: ["^build", "build"]`, so CI is fine, but to reproduce locally run `pnpm --filter @better-auth/core build` first. Pre-existing, not introduced here.
- **Doc snippets are not type-checked in CI** — the docs use no twoslash, so the new recipes were compiled by hand against the real types.
- **Conflict surface.** #10891 (base `main`) edits `verify.ts` + `verify.test.ts`; #10801 (base `main`) edits `client-resource.ts`. #10248 also edits `verify.ts`, `verify.test.ts` and this doc file, but its base is `next`, so it is not a merge conflict for a `main` PR. The colliding hunks are textually disjoint from this diff's. 17 open PRs touch `oauth-provider.mdx`, so expect doc churn there.

## Deliberately not done

- **`packages/mcp` is untouched.** `requireMcpAuth` and `createMcpProtectedRequestHandler` still declare `jwksUrl?: string` and do not accept `jwksCacheKey`, so this issue is only partially addressed. Widening mcp needs its own change.
- **No in-process default.** Auto-resolving the key set from the co-located JWT plugin is a behavior change, not a type widening. The default chain is unchanged — a caller still passes the function.
- **No new export from `core/src/oauth2/index.ts`.** Deliberate: it keeps this diff free of overlap with #11380.
- **Pre-existing `500` instead of `401`.** When a resolver returns a falsy key set, `verify.ts` throws `Error: No jwks found`, which is not an `APIError`, so the resource-server challenge path returns `undefined` and a route handler reports a `500` rather than a `401` with an RFC 6750 challenge. Same for a string source pointing at a bad url. Pre-existing and out of scope; the docs now state the behavior plainly. Worth its own issue.
- **`TypeError` and `JWSInvalid` from a resolver are swallowed** as "probably an opaque token" and fall through to `remoteVerify` when configured, failing closed with a `401` when it is not. Also pre-existing and shared with the string path. Now documented on the option rather than silently surprising.

## Spec

All three surfaces verify the same thing — that the bearer token was issued by the trusted authorization server, using that issuer's signing keys. See RFC 6750 §3, RFC 9068 §4, RFC 7662 §2, RFC 7009 §2.1. The divergence between the surfaces was a Better Auth implementation gap, not a spec requirement.

Closes #11784 bot sync PR; its head is `main`, so it can't take the conflict resolution ## Evidence - **Before:** #11784 is `CONFLICTING`. Merging `origin/main` into `origin/next` stops on 5 conflicts, then 6 more after main moved. **After:** `pnpm typecheck` passes. `vitest run` in `packages/oauth-provider` passes 1181 tests in 48 files, and `packages/core/src/oauth2` passes 177 tests. After the v1.7.10 merge, the one-tap, last-login-method, and package-exports tests pass (141). `biome check packages/oauth-provider` reports no fixes. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way **Blast Radius:** `next` branch only Use a merge commit, not a squash, so `next` keeps `main`'s history and future syncs don't conflict. --- ## Summary by cubic Syncs `main` into `next` with all merge conflicts resolved, and closes the bot's sync PR #11784, which can't take a resolution commit because its head is `main`. Notable changes coming from `main`: - Consent is kept separate per reference when `postLogin.consentReferenceId` returns no reference for some authorizations (#11801). - Confidential `private_key_jwt` clients can rotate their own signing keys at `POST /oauth2/client/rotate-keys` (#11695). - DPoP proofs now work for route-param endpoints and trailing-slash URLs (#11786, #11804). - JWKS key sets are refetched at most once every 30 seconds per process for unknown key IDs, with a 5-second timeout; a newer cached set wins over a pending fetch (#11805, #11810). - Unknown `client_id`s report `client not found`, the token endpoint returns `invalid_client` for an unregistered client, and PKCE verifier mismatches return 400 `invalid_grant` (#11799, #11811, #11176, #11724). - Dynamic registration keeps the requested grants the server supports, so Claude's MCP connector can register (#11797). - Unverifiable JWT access tokens and unreachable JWKS key sets now produce proper errors instead of a 500 or an invalid-token 401 (#11596, #11612). - Device-code clients can refresh for any approved resource after polling with a subset (#11815). - Google One Tap now honors plugin-level `autoSelect`/`cancelOnTapOutside`, applies the Google provider's `mapProfileToUser`/`getUserInfo`, and stops calling FedCM-unsupported prompt methods; `lastLoginMethod` records One Tap sign-ins as `"google"` (#11393, #11696, #11819–#11821). - Package subpath exports are kept in sync with build entries, including the new `better-auth/plugins/one-tap` subpath (#11822), alongside the v1.7.10 release. - MongoDB `findMany` sorts by `id` correctly; mutations of trusted clients return 400 instead of 500; `http` loopback redirect URIs infer as `native`. items.body: Brings stable fixes from main into the next branch. **This PR must be merged by a maintainer using 'Create a merge commit'** (not squash, not rebase). This preserves individual fix commits and their verified signatures. If there are conflicts, resolve them by keeping next's versions for `package.json` files (next is always ahead of main in version numbers). --- ## Summary by cubic Brings stable fixes from `main` into `next`. Must be merged by a maintainer using 'Create a merge commit' to preserve individual fix commits and their verified signatures. - Adds client key rotation: `private_key_jwt` clients with inline `jwks` can now replace their own signing keys at `POST /oauth2/client/rotate-keys`, authenticated by a client assertion addressed to that endpoint. Off by default via `allowClientKeyRotation`; the provider refuses to start with it on the memory adapter or with `generateId: "serial"`. Rotation assertions are accepted when `baseURL` ends in a slash. - Dynamic registration now keeps the requested grants the server supports instead of rejecting the whole registration with `invalid_client_metadata`; unsupported grants are dropped and the response lists the granted ones. A request sharing no grant with the server is still rejected, and `createOAuthClient`/`adminCreateOAuthClient` remain strict. - Fixes DPoP proof validation so the expected `htu` matches the URL the client actually requested: plugin endpoint route params and trailing slashes when `skipTrailingSlashes` is on no longer cause `invalid_dpop_proof`. - Adds black-box DPoP smoke tests that derive `htu` from real client requests via `oauth4webapi`, covering proxies, custom base paths, and trailing-slash setups. - With `clientRegistrationDefaultApplicationType: "infer"`, clients registering `http` callbacks on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `[::1]` without `application_type` now register as `native` instead of being rejected as `web`. This covers older Claude Code releases. - Fixes attempts to update, delete, or rotate the secret of a `cachedTrustedClients` client returning HTTP 500 instead of 400. - Reports an unknown `client_id` as `client not found` across `/oauth2/authorize`, `/oauth2/token`, `/oauth2/revoke`, and `/oauth2/introspect`, including requests that authenticate with a `private_key_jwt` client assertion. The token endpoint now returns `invalid_client` instead of `invalid_grant` for a client that is not registered on the `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, and device code grants. - Treats JWT access tokens that fail verification as unknown tokens on `/oauth2/userinfo`, `/oauth2/introspect`, and `/oauth2/revoke`: a bad signature, `alg: none`, unknown `kid`, or wrong issuer previously returned an empty 500. Valid JWT and opaque tokens are unaffected, and this also covers JWT-shaped tokens when `disableJwtPlugin` is set. - Fixes PKCE token error codes: a `code_verifier` that does not match the authorization's `code_challenge` now returns HTTP 400 `invalid_grant` instead of HTTP 401 `invalid_request`. For optional-PKCE clients, a missing or unexpected `code_verifier` still returns `invalid_request`, now with HTTP 400. - Keeps consent separate per reference: an approval without a reference no longer overwrites consent stored for another reference, and an empty string counts as no reference. Users may see the consent prompt once for authorizations previously approved under another reference. - Limits JWKS refetches for unknown key IDs to once per 30 seconds per process instead of once per token, closes concurrent verifications into one fetch, and fails key set fetches that take over 5 seconds with a `JWKSTimeout` error. A verification joining a pending fetch first reuses any newer cached set. Tokens signed with newly published keys still verify without waiting out the cache. - Reports an unreachable key set as an error instead of an invalid token: verification with `jwksUrl` or `jwks.remoteUrl` now throws when the set cannot be reached, and no longer falls back to remote introspection with `remoteVerify`. The OAuth provider's `/oauth2/introspect`, `/oauth2/userinfo`, and `/oauth2/revoke` return 500 in this case. - Fixes the MongoDB adapter ignoring `sortBy: { field: "id" }`, which could repeat or skip rows when paging. - Refactors the Next.js demo so the server URL, MCP resource URL, and organization claim are shared from `demo/nextjs/lib/demo-url.ts`. - Forces both orderings of the refresh-token revoke vs rotate race in tests instead of relying on scheduling (GHSA-392p-2q2v-4372). - Device-code clients that request `offline_access` and poll the token endpoint for only some approved resources can now refresh for any approved resource; previously a refresh for a resource left out of the poll failed with `invalid_target`. - The Google One Tap prompt no longer calls `getSkippedReason()`, which FedCM doesn't support. A skipped prompt now ends the flow and calls `onPromptNotification` immediately instead of retrying; dismissed prompts still retry. - One Tap now applies the Google provider's `mapProfileToUser` and custom `getUserInfo`, like the standard Google sign-in. Users created through One Tap get the mapped fields, and returning users are updated when `overrideUserInfoOnSignIn` or `account.accountLinking.updateUserInfoOnLink` is on. - One Tap options set on `oneTapClient()` (`autoSelect`, `cancelOnTapOutside`) now apply to the prompt and the Sign in with Google button; values passed to `oneTap()` still override them. - `lastLoginMethod` now records Google One Tap sign-ins as `"google"`, matching the standard Google button; previously One Tap recorded nothing. - Adds `better-auth/plugins/one-tap`, `better-auth/plugins/captcha`, and `better-auth/plugins/open-api` subpath exports so those plugins import like others; previously these imports failed with a "not exported" error, and imports from `better-auth/plugins` and `better-auth/client/plugins` are unchanged. Also fixes `better-auth/plugins/multi-session` and `better-auth/test` type resolution for TypeScript projects using `"moduleResolution": "node"`. If there are conflicts, keep `next`'s versions for `package.json` files. Written for commit b734a418bfade81efd19c3277dc58da6967081b7. Summary will update on new commits.

<!-- release-notes-draft -->
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Keep this PR in Draft. Run `/release-notes` to generate and review the release notes.
> The release bot marks the PR ready when the preview matches the current head. Do not manually mark it ready.

This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## better-auth@1.7.16

### Patch Changes

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - `/admin/update-user` now requires the new `user:set-phone` permission to change `phoneNumber` or `phoneNumberVerified`. If you use a custom access control, add `set-phone` to your statements and grant it to roles that should change phone numbers.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Anonymous users are no longer linked or deleted on a sign-in that is still waiting for a second factor.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Email verification and change email links now only work for the account they were issued to. Opening a change email link no longer signs the user in, and it verifies the new email only if the current one was verified.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Wildcard trusted origins now match custom-scheme URLs by their parsed scheme, host, and path, and no longer match a URL with userinfo or one that cannot be parsed as an origin. A wildcard host made only of digits, dots, and wildcards, such as `192.168.*.*`, now matches only IPv4 addresses in that range.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Looking up a user by email now returns only an account whose stored address matches the requested one, ignoring case, even on databases with accent-insensitive collations. The email OTP password reset routes now validate the address and send the code to the address on the account.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Email change codes from the email OTP plugin are now bound to the requesting account and the new address. Codes sent before the upgrade must be requested again.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Fixed the email OTP `checkVerificationOtp` and `resetPassword` endpoints and the phone number `resetPassword` endpoint allowing more OTP guesses than `allowedAttempts` when requests arrive concurrently. A correct check still leaves the OTP usable for the follow-up call.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - The Expo authorization proxy now sets the signed state cookie only for an unexpired state issued by the server. `getAuthStateVerificationIdentifier` is now exported for plugins that look up OAuth state records.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Passkey registration, device authorization, two-factor enrollment and verification, social account linking, and phone number changes now reject a session revoked in the database or secondary storage, even when cookie caching is enabled. Sessions created from API keys are refused on these routes, except two-factor enrollment and phone number changes.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Generic OAuth providers whose discovery document has a `jwks_uri` now reject a user profile whose `sub` differs from the ID token's `sub`. Direct ID-token sign-in and linking with a generic OAuth provider now resolve the profile from the verified ID token only and ignore a submitted access or refresh token.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Pending organization invitations are now only returned to members whose role can create invitations, and creator-role invitations only to members who hold that role.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Organization invitations use random IDs when `advanced.database.generateId` is not set, including on adapters with sequential default IDs such as MongoDB. On MongoDB, new invitation IDs are strings instead of ObjectIds.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Dynamic access control roles reused through `hasPermission`'s `useMemoryCache` option are now cached per request and per auth instance instead of in a process-global cache, so role changes apply on the next request.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Organization role lists are now trimmed and split on commas wherever they are stored or compared, and invitations with an empty role are rejected.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - With the phone number plugin, `updateUserInfoOnLink` no longer copies an unverified `phoneNumber` from the linked provider's profile. An existing verified number is kept.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - With `requireVerification`, phone number password reset now works only for a verified number. No reset code is sent to an unverified number, and `resetPassword` returns `PHONE_NUMBER_PENDING_VERIFICATION` without adding or changing a password.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - With the phone number plugin, a new user no longer stores a `phoneNumber` that was not verified. Sign-up and sign-in routes reject one sent in the request, and a number from a social profile or in `data` passed to `createUser` is dropped unless it is marked verified.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Phone number verification and password reset codes are now stored under their own namespaces, so a phone number request can no longer create, consume or delete verification codes that belong to other flows. Codes sent before the upgrade must be requested again.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - Account linking and new OAuth users now count an email as verified only when the provider claim is `true` or the string `"true"`, which covers generic OAuth, Cognito, and Microsoft Entra ID claims sent as strings. Any other `emailVerified` value, including a non-boolean value returned from `mapProfileToUser` such as `1`, now reads as unverified.

- [#12198](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12198) [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e) Thanks [@bytaesu](https://github.com/bytaesu)! - With secondary storage, revoking all of a user's sessions or deleting the user now also ends sessions missing from the cached session list.

- Updated dependencies [[`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e), [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e), [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e), [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e), [`f25081a`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/f25081ac0476a9a4295f7a9736ae7239974c7b1e)]:

items.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Closed without merging. Giving a client an owner at first consent hands control of a registration to the first organization that approves it, even when other organizations use it. Organizations that use a client are recorded per consent with `postLogin.consentReferenceId`, now documented in #11831. The CIMD refresh fix ships on its own in #11830.

## Summary

With `allowUnauthenticatedClientRegistration`, a client such as a desktop or CLI AI assistant registers itself at install time. Today it can obtain tokens as soon as any user consents, and it belongs to nobody: no organization sees it in its client list or can update or delete it, and its tokens cannot carry an organization. The opt-in `approvePendingClient` option holds these clients until a signed-in user consents, and gives the client an owner at that moment, typically the organization the user administers.

```text
open registration (no session, no initial access token)
  store client with pending = true
    must register authorization_code, else invalid_client_metadata
    may request client_credentials, unusable until an admin assigns its scopes
token, refresh, introspect, revoke, device authorization, private_key_jwt
  pending client → invalid_client
authorize
  pending client → consent page (even with skipConsent; prompt=none → consent_required)
consent accepted
  approvePendingClient({ client, user, session, scopes, consentReferenceId, headers })
    false → redirect to the client with access_denied, nothing stored
    APIError → returned to the consent page, nothing stored
    { clientReference }
      one transaction: approve only if still pending and unowned (else 409), then store consent
```

Decisions a reviewer cannot see in the diff:

- **Discovered clients are never pending.** A client ID metadata document identifies software that every user and organization runs, so the first organization to approve it would own it. An owner can change the client's redirect URIs or delete it, which would affect everyone. The docs give the same limit for open registration: approve only clients that one organization uses.
- **Approval assigns only the owner.** The `client_credentials` scope limit is still set through `adminUpdateOAuthClient`, with `clientPrivileges` approving `configure-client-credentials-scopes`, as for every other client.
- **`clientReference` is required.** With a default owner, a callback that returned `{}` would hand any client to any signed-in user.
- **A refusal redirects like a denied consent** ([RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749.html#section-4.1.2.1)), so the client is not left waiting.
- Registration responses and the public client endpoints return `pending: true`, so the consent page can tell the user the client is being handed to an owner. [RFC 7591 §5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7591.html#section-5) leaves trust in dynamically registered clients to the server.
- For every app, a CIMD refresh no longer rewrites the scope limit, `disabled`, `skipConsent`, or `enableEndSession` from its pre-fetch snapshot, so an administrator's change committed during the fetch is kept.

Without the option, behavior is unchanged. The PR adds a nullable `pending` column to `oauthClient`, so it is `minor` and targets `next`.

## Evidence

- **Before:** an ownerless self-registered client could get tokens at once.
  **After:** `packages/oauth-provider/src/client-approval.test.ts` and `packages/cimd/src/flows.test.ts`:

```text
open registration, option on              → pending; token, client_credentials → invalid_client
registration with only client_credentials → 400 invalid_client_metadata
initial access token registration         → not pending
CIMD discovery, option on                 → not pending, no owner, code issued, callback not called
approve { clientReference }               → owner set, consent stored, code exchanged
                                            client_credentials still refused
  then adminUpdateOAuthClient assigns scopes → client_credentials issued
approve false                             → redirect with access_denied and state; still pending, no consent
approve {}                                → 500; still pending, no consent
approve with generateId: "serial"         → owner set
two concurrent approvals                  → 200 and 409, one owner
CIMD refresh racing an admin's scope limit and disable → both kept
```

Restoring CIMD pending fails both discovery tests, and making a refusal throw again fails the redirect test. The oauth-provider (1247) and cimd (209) suites pass on SQLite, and both packages typecheck.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way

Users run a migration for the `pending` column, and pending clients stay blocked if the option is later removed.

**Blast Radius:** opt-in

- **Shared registrations:** an owner can edit or delete its client. An app that approves an open registration used by several organizations hands that control to the first approver; the docs say to register such clients with `adminCreateOAuthClient`.
- **Prisma on MongoDB:** pending clients store `referenceId` as null so approval's null filter matches. This adapter was not run.
- **Adapters:** the approval suite ran on SQLite only. Without transaction support, a failed consent write can leave a client approved without a consent row; consenting again recovers.
- Pending clients never expire.
